title: ‘It pissed him off’: New Eagles freak vows to show NFL teams what they ‘missed out on’
description: Eagles defender is motivated by offseason disrespect: "It pissed him off.'
fullText:
PHILADELPHIA — After being introduced as UTSA's cornerbacks coach in 2020, Nick Graham was told by another coach on the staff to watch Riq Woolen's tape from his first few practices at cornerback from the year before.

On that day, Graham discovered the best cornerback talent he had ever seen as a coach. Woolen had practiced as a cornerback for only one week during the 2019 season. He was still listed as a wide receiver on UTSA's roster.

Right away, Graham was enamored by Woolen's size (6-foot-4, 210 pounds), his elite speed and smooth hips. Not long after watching Woolen's film for the first time, Graham convinced Woolen to switch from wide receiver to cornerback.

"I go watch this tape and go, 'Whoa, God, I don't know what I did to deserve this, but thank you,'" Graham told NJ.com last week.

Graham is confident the Eagles will be thanking the rest of the NFL for allowing them to sign Woolen to a one-year, $12 million contract on March 10.

The Eagles are listed at +215 to win over 11.5 regular season games next season on DraftKings. Our complete DraftKings Sportsbook review provides a useful guide on how to navigate their app. Also, make sure to view our Eagles win total prediction for next season for a full expert breakdown.

Woolen, who was drafted by the Seattle Seahawks in the fifth round, was one of the NFL's best rookies in 2022, and over the last four years, he has proven to be one of the NFL's most talented cornerbacks. However, Woolen has not always been consistent, and that has gotten him into trouble.

Still, the way Graham sees it, Woolen is on the verge of a breakout.

"I think the Eagles got a steal, and I think they know it. I know they know it," Graham said.

Woolen's signing also carried personal meaning for Graham, whose own playing career began with the Eagles. Graham played his rookie season for the Eagles in 2007 as a backup cornerback and special-teams contributor. He knows what it's like to play in Philadelphia, and he is confident Woolen is a perfect fit.

"I texted Riq, 'I know you're (expletive) lying,'" Graham said about his reaction to the Eagles signing Woolen. "That was the first thing I said to him. He was like, 'Coach Graham, can you believe it? Can you believe I'm playing where you used to play?' I was just excited for him because I know the type of organization [the Eagles are]. I know the defense that is there. Man, I'm just excited for the kid. I really am."

Graham's excitement has not worn off since. He was shocked the Eagles were able to add Woolen to one of the NFL's best secondaries.

Woolen is receiving a fresh start with the Eagles, and Graham believes a change of scenery will unlock Woolen's talent.

The Seahawks benched Woolen multiple times over the last three years. He played 817 defensive snaps last year, the fewest of his career.

"He's not a finished product, but I believe he has gold jacket ability," Graham said.

Woolen, 27, has made one Pro Bowl, but Graham believes he can become a Hall of Fame-caliber player.

"Athletically, he's there, but just knowledge of the game and just mastering his technique and his craft, I don't think that he's there yet," Graham said. "And I think that when he puts that all together, I just don't know [if there is anyone better]. There may be three in the league that I could say, 'Oh, yeah, they're better.'

"And so, I just think that he has a rare skill set. I can go another 20 years, and I'll never coach an athlete like that. When he puts that all together, I think it's going to be scary hours."

It took some convincing, but Woolen is glad he was receptive to Graham's advice to play cornerback.

"I feel like it helped make me be the person I am today, and it shows that I can go through adversity, go through a whole position change and still become great," Woolen told NJ.com after Monday's training camp practice.

Woolen dealt with a shoulder injury in 2023 and was benched for a Week 15 game against the Eagles that year. He was also benched in 2024 for the opening drive against the Minnesota Vikings after violating undisclosed team rules.

Last season, Woolen drew a taunting penalty in the NFC Championship Game that nearly proved costly. On the next play, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua beat him for a 34-yard touchdown, cutting Los Angeles' deficit to four points at 31-27.

But Woolen will not let those tough moments define him.

"Whenever you're making progress, it's like a roller coaster," Woolen said. "It's loops in all different ways, but you still gotta ascend. As long as you are still ascending, then you're doing the right things."

Despite being one of the best young talents available this offseason, Woolen received no long-term offers in free agency.

According to Next Gen Stats, Woolen allowed only 0.5 yards per coverage snap in man coverage, the lowest among outside cornerbacks. He also allowed a 31.3% completion rate in man coverage, the lowest among cornerbacks.

"I guarantee you it pissed him off," Graham said about Woolen not landing a big deal. "To me, he's a $20 million a year guy talent-wise."

Woolen admitted that not receiving big offers gives him extra motivation, but he's happy to be in a place where his career could take off.

"My whole thing is just getting everything down, being a great teammate, showing these guys that they can ride with me and be consistent," Woolen said. "Whenever the season comes, every week, I'll get my chance to prove to everybody else what they missed out on."

Graham doesn't think Seattle was the best place to develop Woolen.

"Going in and out like he was doing last year, nobody wants to do that," Graham said about Woolen rotating with Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe last year. "I don't think he's that type of player that needs to be doing that. And so, he's always confident, but I just think it's the love you receive. We're all humans. We want to be somewhere where we know that people care about us."

Woolen's new Eagles teammates and coaches have spoken highly of his abilities. Woolen will start this season across from All-Pro Quinyon Mitchell.

"To be here and to know that I have a role and I have a role that plays a big part in this team, it's a blessing for real," Woolen said. "Because that's something that I want, and that's something that I will excel at."

Woolen is best as a man-coverage cornerback, and the Eagles play more man coverage than Seattle does. Last year, the Eagles played man coverage on 24.5% of their snaps, while Seattle did so on 15.2%, according to Sharp Football Analysis.

'Don't want to b****': Eagles star won't let how he's been treated ruin potential farewell seasonAug. 9, 2026, 6:30 a.m.

Massive Eagles rookie turning heads as superstar's potential heir: 'He's going to be a big problem'Aug. 10, 2026, 2:46 p.m.

Although Graham believes that Woolen will be targeted the most among the Eagles' cornerbacks, he expects Woolen to prove he is a top player at the position.

To Graham, nobody deserves that success more.

"He's the nicest kid ever, man," Graham said. "He loves his family, Got a great mama, great brother and sister. He just takes care of everybody. And he's the same person every day. There ain't a vindictive bone in his body. He's a good kid. He's always a pleasure to be around. Every time we talk, it's 'I love you.' I mean it, and I know that he means it. And so me and that kid will always have a special bond."

title: Los Angeles Chargers news: When should we worry about Rashawn Slater?
description: Chargers LT Rashawn Slater has missed 3 consecutive practices while no reason has been given for his absence as of yet.
fullText:
Left tackle Rashawn Slater missed practice for the third consecutive day on Monday, despite Jim Harbaugh telling reporters that he was "right on track" returning from his torn patellar tendon. That injury happened on August 7th of last year, marking a full calendar year since the event.

Saturday's absence was due to a veteran's rest day, per Harbaugh. But here we are two practices past that and he still has not returned to the field.

Do we think it is the normal caution the team has shown with their stars over in recent years? Whatever it is, I believe a fourth missed practice will be one of the justifiable tipping points for fans to start worrying about their star tackle.

title: Notts County sign Samuels-Smith and Mustapha on loan
description: Notts County sign Ishe Samuels-Smith and Hindolo Mustapha on season-long loan deals.
fullText:
Notts County have signed Ishe Samuels-Smith and Hindolo Mustapha on season-long loan deals.

Samuels-Smith, 20, joins from Chelsea and can play different roles on the left side of defence, while Mustapha joins from Crystal Palace after cutting short a loan spell with Wigan Athletic.

The 20-year-old attacking midfielder has been capped by Sierra Leone at international level. Samuels-Smith has represented England at Under-20 level.

The pair move to the Magpies as they embark on their first season back in League One since 2014-15.

"Ishe is a talented young player who is capable of contributing in both attacking and defensive phases," County director of football Richard Montague told the club website.

Montague added Mustapha was one of the club's "top targets this summer".

title: Ranking every Power 4 college football team in California
description: Which Power 4 school in California will lead the way in 2026?
fullText:
Who's the best college football team in California? It's a question that seems to be repetitive each season.

With the season just under one month away, there might not be a better time than now to decide which school reigns supreme heading into the 2026 season.

Jul 28, 2026; Chicago, IL, USA; USC football head coach Lincoln Riley speaks during Media Days at Hilton Chicago. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images

Are they from the ACC or the Big Ten?

Maybe to some fans, it might not even be any of the teams listed, but for the sake of time, we've decided to rank only the Power 4 conference teams: the ACC, Big Ten, SEC, and Big 12.

MORE: Why UCLA football gave Derek Carr a coaching title with no paycheck attached

Coming into the 2026 campaign, the UCLA Bruins look to turn the page on last year's three-win season, bringing in new leadership as former James Madison head coach Bob Chesney takes the reins at UCLA.

Likely to deploy Nico Iamaleava as the starter once again, UCLA saw significant roster turnover in several other position groups, bringing in 40-plus transfers this offseason.

UCLA also has a graceful schedule for 2026, with the Bruins playing nine games on the West Coast, eight of them in-state.

It's an alumni party in Stanford as Tavita Pritchard will be in the head coaching role for his alma mater.

Alongside team general manager Andrew Luck, another former Stanford quarterback, Pritchard will look to restore their school's glory and out of the bottom of their conference

Bringing on a new arm for Stanford, Davis Warren transferred from Michigan blue to Cardinal red after missing the entire 2025 season due to a torn ACL.

Now recovered, Warren hopes to find the same spark he displayed in 2024, and with work alongside Pritchard and Luck, perhaps he could be the driving force who shifts the tide in Stanford.

Outside of our No. 1 team for this list, there might not be a team on the West Coast with more hype to have a breakout season than the California Golden Bears.

Finishing in the middle of the ACC last year, Cal showed the college football world that it was no longer going to sit and watch but was back to being competitive.

With Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele entering his second year under center, plus Cal alum Tosh Lupoi taking over the head coaching duties, the Golden Bears may be on the cusp of being one of the top teams in the ACC for 2026.

Can this be the season Lincoln Riley finally delivers in the College Football Playoff?

The Trojans are certainly built for it behind potential first-round quarterback Jayden Maiava, who led USC to a nine-win season last year.

Losing several key stars to the NFL draft could impact USC. However, with 10 transfers joining the team and expected to make an impact, such as wide receiver Terrell Anderson and defensive lineman Alex VanSumeren, the Trojans' roster is still ready to break the glass ceiling as a contender.

title: J.J. McCarthy landing spots: Chargers, Buccaneers among best fits should Vikings trade recently named backup QB
description: J.J. McCarthy will start the season behind Kyler Murray, unless the Vikings decide to trade him.
fullText:
J.J. McCarthy landing spots: Chargers, Buccaneers among best fits should Vikings trade recently named backup QB originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Vikings named Kyler Murray their starting quarterback on Tuesday, ending the battle between the former Cardinals starter and J.J. McCarthy before any preseason games were played.

McCarthy was always going to face an uphill battle to becoming the Vikings' Week 1 starter after a difficult 2025. Now, questions about his future will begin to swirl after a quick decision from Kevin O'Connell.

If the Vikings decide to trade McCarthy, where could he go?

Here are the top landing spots for the former first-round pick after he was beaten out for Minnesota's starting job.

MORE:Why Vikings named Kyler Murray starter before preseason

The connection here is obvious. Jim Harbaugh coached McCarthy to great success at Michigan, and much of his staff is also familiar with the young quarterback. The Chargers, of course, wouldn't be able to give McCarthy a path to a starting job, but he might not be in any position to demand one at this point.

A trade to the Chargers would give McCarthy the opportunity to get back to basics under a coach he already knows well and learn from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. The Chargers have a low-end backup in Trey Lance, so a deal for McCarthy could be a worthwhile flier if his value is low enough.

The Buccaneers would be a nice fit for McCarthy for two reasons: Jake Browning isn't a particularly inspiring option behind Baker Mayfield, and Mayfield's future in Tampa Bay is up in the air after he blasted the organization for its latest contract offer. The Buccaneers could simply franchise tag Mayfield in the offseason, but it's possible the dynamic between the two becomes untenable. If that's the case, having an option with some upside already on the roster couldn't hurt.

MORE:Projecting the NFL's next 10 Hall of Fame QBs

Like L.A., Buffalo isn't a place where McCarthy could ever dream of starting as long as Josh Allen is alive and well. The Bills don't have a particularly exciting or high-ceiling backup, however, as Kyle Allen is locked into the No. 2 role in 2026. Spending a couple of years learning from a former MVP could rehab McCarthy's image even if he doesn't ever see the field.

McCarthy overlapped with new Ravens head coach Jesse Minter at Michigan, where Minter ran the defense. That connection, plus the need for a backup plan behind Lamar Jackson, could make the fit ideal. Tyler Huntley is back as Baltimore's No. 2 quarterback, but he's bounced around over the last couple of years and didn't have any familiarity with Minter before this offseason.

MORE:Ranking the 28 'modern-era' QBs in Hall of Fame

The Lions lost backup Teddy Bridgewater to retirement over the weekend. While Detroit was quick to sign Josh Dobbs, who by all accounts is a capable No. 2, McCarthy would give Dan Campbell a higher-ceiling backup option and even a potential long-term solution behind Jared Goff if one was necessary, as far-fetched as that scenario might be. Would the Vikings be willing to trade McCarthy within the division? That's more uncertain.

The Jaguars are content with Trevor Lawrence as their starting quarterback, but they have one of the worst backup situations in the NFL with Nick Mullens as their No. 2. Working with offensive guru Liam Coen would give McCarthy a chance to rehab his reputation, and Lawrence takes enough risks that seeing the field as a backup in Jacksonville isn't inconceivable by any means.

title: Celtic Eye Summer Move For This Veteran Newcastle United Custodian: Should He Replace Sinisalo As The Hoops ‘Number 1’?
description: If a recent report from The Daily Mail (as cited by The Daily Express) is believed to be true, Celtic are keeping close tabs on Nick Pope ahead of a potential summer move. But they are not alone in th...
fullText:
If a recent report from The Daily Mail (as cited by The Daily Express) is believed to be true, Celtic are keeping close tabs on Nick Pope ahead of a potential summer move. But they are not alone in the race, with Premier League newcomers  Ipswich Town also eyeing a move for the Newcastle United goalkeeper.

The 34-year-old England international progressed through Ipswich Town's academy ranks before leaving his boyhood side for non-league outfit Bury Town. Charlton secured his services in the summer of 2011; however, he was primarily loaned out to Harrow Borough, Welling United, Cambridge United, Aldershot Town, York City and Bury in the lower leagues to gain first-team experience. An impressive 2015-16 campaign for the Addicks in the Championship earned him a £1.1m transfer to then newly-promoted Premier League outfit Burnley.

After spending the first season as the understudy to Tom Heaton, Pope cemented a starting status between the sticks and went on to feature 155 times for the Clarets before securing a £10m switch to the Magpies in 2022. Despite being the preferred option in the last line of defence, the Three Lions veteran has struggled at times due to form and fitness reasons. Newcastle have splashed a combined fee of around £45m for Lukáš Horníček and Ewen Jaouen, respectively, from Braga and Reims, thus making him surplus to requirements under new boss Matthias Jaissle.

LONDON, ENGLAND – FEBRUARY 10: Nick Pope of Newcastle United punches the ball during the Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on February 10, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

Celtic have made an electrifying start to their Premiership title defence with back-to-back wins against Dundee and Kilmarnock. They have opted for quality over quantity, with Camilo Duran and Kasper Høgh being the only arrivals so far this window. Martin O'Neill has banked on Viljami Sinisalo since Kasper Schmeichel's season-ending shoulder injury, which eventually forced the Dane to retire upon the closure of the previous campaign.

Although the Finnish shot-stopper has retained the 'number 1' spot, the Celts have opted for an experienced, established figure over a younger alternative in the recent past. Schmeichel was brought in as a like-for-like replacement for Joe Hart, and it remains to be seen whether they follow a similar strategy before the window is slammed shut.

Pope might prefer a return to his hometown club, but a move north of the border would see him contest for silverware rather than engage in a survival battle. Assured minutes in Europe should further fascinate him to ply his trade in Glasgow, as his expertise in goal could earn him the first-choice status for at least a couple of seasons ahead of Sinisalo.

title: Packers Training Camp Recap: Pass-catchers return to practice
description: WRs Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed returned to practice for the Green Bay Packers, as did TE Josh Whyle
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers are planning on playing healthy starters against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday, according to head coach Matt LaFleur. Before practice on Tuesday, LaFleur stated that even quarterback Jordan Love is expected to play versus the Steelers, though he added that he has the right to change his mind between now and kickoff.

Here's what you missed during the Packers' final practice of preparation leading up to their preseason opener.

Cornerback Domani Jackson's injury has finally been identified. Per LaFleur, Jackson had surgery to his core over the offseason, but he's hopeful that Jackson will "be out there shortly."

Receiver Jayden Reed (ankle), receiver Matthew Golden (toe) and tight end Josh Whyle (neck) all returned to practice today. I think we can all collectively exhale for the status of the pass-catching group. Cornerback Carrington Valentine (hamstring) is also back out on the field.

Running back Josh Jacobs (groin), edge defender Dani Dennis-Sutton (illness) and safety Javon Bullard (foot) join Jackson as injured players on the active list. Meanwhile, tight end Luke Musgrave (neck), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (ankle) and long snapper Matt Orzech (calf) remain on the team's PUP list.

The Packers signed two new safeties, which means that they needed to make two corresponding roster moves. To make room for the new additions, the team released offensive lineman Dylan Barnhart and tight end Drew Biber. Barnhart was a 2025 practice squadder while Biber, a Wisconsin native, was signed to Green Bay just over the last week.

title: Tottenham begin discussions with Monaco for Folarin Balogun
description: According to a report from L’Équipe, Tottenham Hotspur have opened discussions with AS Monaco over a transfer for Folarin Balogun (25), with the French outlet writing that the striker is estimated ...
fullText:
According to a report from L'Équipe, Tottenham Hotspur have opened discussions with AS Monaco over a transfer for Folarin Balogun (25), with the French outlet writing that the striker is estimated to be worth around €60m.

Balogun is coming off his third season in the Principality, having moved to the Ligue 1 side from Tottenham's rivals Arsenal in 2023. The US international has been linked this summer with an exit. Spanish and English sides (including Newcastle United) have reportedly held an interest in a striker, who scored 19 times across 45 games last season.

Balogun made headlines at the 2026 FIFA World Cup when his red card suspension was lifted in time for the Round of 16 exit to Belgium. The striker had been sent off in the Round of 32, but this was overturned following a call from US President Donald Trump, who made a call pleading Balogun's case, albeit FIFA denies that this had any sway on the final decision.

title: Here is the first Seahawks unofficial depth chart for 2026
description: The Seahawks have their 90-man depth chart ready for preseason… unofficially, of course.
fullText:
It's a Seattle Seahawks (preseason) game week, which also means we get to see the team's first unofficial depth chart for the 2026 season.

Ahead of Seattle's preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys, the Seahawks unveiled their 90-man roster in depth chart form. Have a look for yourself!

A couple of things to note when reading the Seahawks depth chart:

Nick Emmanwori is now off of PUP after passing his physical, so this time next week the depth chart will look different. The unofficial depth chart was obviously finalized before Tuesday morning.

If you want to know about ordinal ranking on a depth chart, read from left to right by row. For example, the cornerback room behind Devon Witherspoon would read: Nehemiah Pritchett, Shemar Jean-Charles, Michael Dansby, and Andre Fuller.

Just in case it hasn't been emphasized already, this is an unofficial depth chart, so don't make too many grand declarations or worry about the fact that nearly all of the Seahawks rookies are buried in the back-end. That's not uncommon for the Seahawks and probably not for many other teams.

I can say that after a week of Seahawks training camp, and acknowledging that some players listed on here missed practice, that there's a healthy set of accuracy attached to this depth chart. Pritchett and Igbinoghene have definitely had the bulk of the snaps with the ones and twos, and they look odds-on to make the roster. The running back room is very much a by-committee situation until further notice, so I wouldn't read too much into Holani RB1 (especially once Zach Charbonnet returns). Logan Brown and Amari Kight, for example, have hopped between the second and third teams while working either tackle spot. Shaheed and Horton have worked with both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. Elijah Arroyo has had 11-on-11 reps with Darnold, Lock, and Milroe but obviously he's much more of a receiving tight end in 12 personnel looks than Eric Saubert.

The only eyebrow raiser to me is Rodney Thomas listed behind A.J. Finley, although in hindsight we've seen a lot of Finley and Maxen Hook with the second unit. There have been some three-safety looks in which Thomas is involved with the twos, so that competition is very tight.

We'll definitely have a better feel for Seattle's depth chart—realistically, the non-starters—once preseason games get underway.

title: Ramsay-Peaty fifth in European Championships 100m final
description: Adam Ramsay-Peaty was beaten for the first time at a European Aquatics Championships as he finished fifth in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.
fullText:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty was beaten for the first time at a European Aquatics Championships as he finished fifth in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.

The 31-year-old, who has 16 European Championships golds, had previously never lost a heat, semi-final or final at the event.

Olympic champion Nicolo Martinenghi won the race in 58.58 seconds, with Ivan Kozhakin finishing second and Italy's Simone Cerasuolo third.

Ramsay-Peaty finished 0.01secs and one place ahead of Great Britain team-mate Filip Nowacki.

The three-time Olympic champion, who is the 100m breaststroke world record holder, said "nothing makes sense" after a disappointing Commonwealth Games last month, where he won two bronze medals.

His time of 59.10 in Paris was 0.55secs faster than at the Commonwealth Games, where he was beaten by 18-year-old Nowacki, who made history for Jersey by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke in Glasgow.

Ramsay-Peaty later took part in Great Britain's mixed 4x100m medley relay final, swimming an impressive split of 58.9 in the breaststroke leg, but the team finished fourth.

Elsewhere at the championships, Great Britain's Katie Shanahan dominated the 200m backstroke to win gold by 1.49secs with a time of two minutes 06.13secs.

The 22-year-old won silver in the same race at the 2022 European Aquatics Championships in Rome.

GB's Angharad Evans, 23, also claimed a new championship record in the women's 100m breaststroke semi-final with a time of 1:04.97.

title: 'He's a thumper': Texas A&M DC heaps immense praise on transfer LB
description: New Texas A&M DC Lyle Hemphill praised transfer LB Ray Coney's athleticism and football IQ during Tuesday's presser.
fullText:
Texas A&M completed its fifth preseason practice on Monday, and plenty of players stood out; redshirt junior quarterback Marcel Reed continued to make strides as a passer, hitting star junior wide receiver Mario Craver in stride while escaping pressure and impressing the coaching staff and every media member in attendance.

This offseason, before a record 10 players were selected in the 2026 NFL Draft, third-year coach Mike Elko and his staff landed 17 players from the transfer portal, including former Tulsa linebacker Ray Coney, who recorded 128 tackles with the Hurricanes last season and is nationally regarded as one of the top run defenders, while possessing the necessary size at 6'2" and 240 pounds.

Paired with sophomore Noah Mikhail and senior Daymion Sanford, Texas A&M's revamped linebacker rotation slowly, but surely looks like one of the program's strengths, and on Tuesday, new defensive coordinator Lyle Hemphill stated that Sanford is "close to 100%" after returning from the fibula injury he suffered during the Maroon & White Game.

Hemphill, who served as a defensive assistant with the Aggies last season, is a rising star in the coaching ranks and had plenty of positive things to say about A&M's linebacker rotation, calling the group "Improved" while singling out Ray Coney, who is on pace to dominate during his first and likely only season in College Station.

"He's everything I thought he'd be. He's 6-1, 240-plus. He's loose and athletic. He's a thumper. You can see why he had the tackles he had."

"Now that he's been here for a minute, he's starting to figure it out. He's going to be a hell of a player."

Coney is listed as 6'2" on the Texas A&M Athletics website, but nonetheless, after losing three-year starting linebacker Taurean York to the NFL, Ray Coney, a healthy Daymion Sanford, and Noah Mikhail taking another step in his development should result in the Aggie linebackers being a consistent force in 2026.

title: The Good, Bad And Ugly From The Packers’ 11th Training Camp Practice
description: The Green Bay Packers held their 11th practice of training camp Tuesday, and had a number of highs and lows.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers held their 11th training camp Tuesday on a gorgeous, 77-degree morning. The practice lasted 1 hour, 32 minutes.

Green Bay now heads to Pittsburgh for its first preseason game of 2026 on Thursday at 6 p.m. (CST). The Packers will meet former coach Mike McCarthy and ex-quarterback Aaron Rodgers — a pair that led the franchise to a win in Super Bowl XLV.

Here's the good, bad and ugly — compiled from multiple reports — from practice No. 11.

PLAY ON: Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said quarterback Jordan Love and the Packers' starters would play at Pittsburgh Thursday.

LaFleur, now in his eighth season, has handled the risk-reward element of playing starters in preseason games both ways. On Monday, though, LaFleur said, "I think just my experiences here is that when we've played in the preseason, we've been better earlier in the season."

LaFleur also noted that data shows when players get at least 30 snaps in the preseason, they're less likely to be injured once the regular season begins.

Green Bay, which ended last season on a five-game losing streak, can't afford a slow start. The Packers face just one playoff team from 2025 in their first seven games, and need to take full advantage of their soft early season schedule.

Critics will scream there's too much risk playing your frontliners in August games. But there's also risk walking down the street or driving to work every day.

Nothing toughens you up and readies you more for the regular season than playing your people. LaFleur clearly feels the same.

"I do think there's a lot of value for all our guys to just get mentally prepared to go play a game, whether it's one play, whether it's three plays, 10 plays, the whole game, I think there's a ton of value in that," LaFleur said. "Just getting your process down."

LOVE > RODGERS: LaFleur made headlines Monday telling the NFL Network that Jordan Love was the best quarterback he's worked with when it comes to pre-snap, line protection calls and adjustments.

Considering LaFleur coached Aaron Rodgers from 2019-2022, that's a bold statement.

On Tuesday, LaFleur doubled down.

"I mean, (Love) is so in tune with everything we're doing, and shoot, it happened today, where he's in there, and we're talking about different looks about what you could do," LaFleur said. "And he said something that I hadn't thought of, and I was like, 'Oh yeah, that's pretty good.'

"So I think he's … really grown in that facet, and he can he has complete command at the line of scrimmage, and then he just, he trusts everything that we talk about in that room, and he goes out there and executes it."

"Aaron was phenomenal too. Don't get me wrong, and I think Jordan really benefited from watching him and how he operated and how quickly he could process things. But I do think our offense has evolved over time too. So that's all I'm going to say about that."
MINOR STRIDES: Rookie kicker Trey Smack went 4-of-5 on field goals and is now 20-of-28 in training camp (71.4%). Smack's effort on Tuesday took his average above 70.0% for the first time this summer.

Smack made kicks from 33, 41, 43 and 45 yards, and was also wide right from 45. Smack's 41-yarder bounced off the right upright and through.

WELCOME BACK: Wide receivers Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (foot) returned to practice, as did tight end Josh Whyle (neck) and cornerback Carrington Valentine (hamstring).

Reed, Golden and Whyle all did team drills, while Valentine worked in the rehab group.

COMINGS AND GOINGS: Green Bay added defensive backs Trey Dean (35) and Tra Fluellen (48) to the roster and released tight end Drew Biber and guard Karsen Barnhart.

THIS AND THAT: Love hit Skyy Moore with an impressive deep ball that went for a big gain. … Ty'Ron Hopper forced a fumble from running back Jaden Nixon. … Edge Lukas Van Ness beat Zach Bako-Bewele, forcing Love to step into a sack from safety Kitan Oladapo.

OFFENSIVE STRUGGLES: Green Bay's defense got the better of the offense, which has been a consistent theme throughout camp.

Love and the offense couldn't get much going until they faced the No. 2 defense late in practice.

While that's good news for the defense, the Packers' struggles on offense should be concerning. Green Bay's offensive line is unsettled, running back Josh Jacobs is out with a groin injury and there's little depth at tight end or wide receiver.

The Packers averaged just 19.2 points per game during their five-game losing streak to end 2025. They'll need to be much better than that when the regular season arrives.

NO ACTION FOR JACKSON: LaFleur said rookie cornerback Domani Jackson, a sixth round draft pick in April, had core muscle surgery in the offseason.

The injury kept Jackson out of the spring and most of training camp.

"He just has been trying to work through some of the stuff, and hopefully he'll be out there shortly," LaFleur said.

FROM THE INFIRMARY: Here's how the Packers' injury list looked Tuesday.

Not practicing: safety Javon Bullard (foot), running back Josh Jacobs (groin), edge Dani Dennis-Sutton (illness) and cornerback Domani Jackson (core). Guard Aaron Banks (knee) was also given a rest day.

Bullard, who was in a walking boot, said Monday his foot injury wasn't anything to worry about long term.

"It's nothing crazy. I'll be back in no time," Bullard said. "If we had a game tomorrow I'd play. It's nothing crazy. We're just trying to proceed with caution right now instead of letting it linger and be dealing with it later on."

As for Jacobs, LaFleur said Tuesday "he's going to be out for at least this week."
Reserve lists: edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee), tight end Luke Musgrave (neck), long snapper Matt Orzech (calf) and defensive tackle Jordon Reilly (Achilles).

THIS AND THAT: Bo Melton dropped a pass from Love that would have gone for a big gain. … Green Bay's running backs had little to no room to get started throughout practice.

GIVE IT UP MATT: Packers coach Matt LaFleur has a career record of just 19-26 when throwing the challenge flag, a dismal winning percentage of.422.

The NFL made a rule change starting this season that allows a designated assistant coach to throw the challenge flag instead of strictly the head coach. Still, LaFleur doesn't plan to give up those duties.

"I probably should give it up based on past actions," LaFleur said with a chuckle Tuesday. "So no, I'll probably hold the challenge flag."

Since the start of 2023, LaFleur has challenged 18 plays. Just five have been overturned, giving him a paltry 27.8% success rate in the last three seasons.

Still, LaFleur said he feels good about the process he's established to challenge plays.

"Where it gets challenging is if you leave, you know, and … if you go talk to the quarterbacks or receivers or whoever or somebody on offense when the defense is out there and you have a bang, bang play," LaFleur said. "Then you just have to have urgency to get up there and throw the flag."

LaFleur has a lot on his plate during game days. And his success rate throwing the flag in recent years has been nightmarish.

Perhaps it's time to pass the torch, or in this case, the flag.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Dave Roberts Calls For Dodgers To Play With More Urgency Amid Standings Slide
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are 208 in their last 10 games
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are 2-10 in their last 10 games despite a very aggressive trade deadline approach.

The offense has been inconsistent, and the bullpen has been a mess. They won on Monday night, but blew a two-run lead to the lowly Kansas City Royals. They are tied with the Atlanta Braves for the second-best record in the National League, and would be playing in a wild card series if the regular season ended today.

"We're a wild-card team right now," manager Dave Roberts said on Monday, per The Athletic's Katie Woo. "We have to get going and play with urgency. We have to make sure we don't get ahead of the playoff situation, and talk about winning now, winning today, winning tomorrow."

The Dodgers are three games back of the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the NL and the best record in baseball. They will take on the Brewers in a four-game series starting on Thursday. That series could decide which team gets the No. 1 seed and will dictate who holds the tiebreaker if they finish with the same record. The Dodgers have a 2-1 lead over the Brewers in the season series right now. The Dodgers' roster is loaded, and it would be easy to assume things will get back on track.

Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand!

"That part of the, 'We're gonna be OK and we're good,' that's not good enough," Roberts said. "Clearly it's not, given how we've played over the last month. We put ourselves in this position. A lot of talent. But I think across the board, we need to play with more urgency. And our guys know that."

The Dodgers have been dealing with some injuries and are getting some guys back. Blake Snell will return on Tuesday, and Tyler Glasnow is on a rehab assignment. Shohei Ohtani has begun a throwing progression in hopes of returning to the mound soon. Getting those three arms in the rotation with Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Roki Sasaki and Justin Wrobleski will be huge for the Dodgers.

title: Saquon Barkley shares one wish for Eagles' offense that might come true this season
description: This one wish from Saquon Barkley could come true this season.
fullText:
Saquon Barkley shares one wish for Eagles' offense that might come true this season originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Philadelphia Eagles did not have a successful 2025 season by any means. While the defense looked good, the offense was a complete mess.

Kevin Patullo's offense just didn't work, and it didn't help that the offensive line was hurt, and players weren't playing well enough. Saquon Barkley was one of the biggest players impacted, as the run game took a massive step back last season.

Amid the struggles, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports Barkley shared a wish for the Eagles' offense that, while it didn't come true last season, should come true in 2026 under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion.

"Running back Saquon Barkley is known as the ultimate good teammate who doesn't create issues internally, but whispers began last year that he would welcome running the ball from under center more often," Fowler reports.

While Fowler isn't reporting that Barkley was doing anything detrimental to the team by wishing for more under-center runs, it's noteworthy the language Fowler used.

Leading up to this wish from Barkley by noting how he's the "ultimate good teammate" implies that this wish from the star running back was a bit out of character.

MORE: Eagles' Jalen Hurts 'shouldn't have trouble' reaching Hall of Fame if he can continue to have playoff success

However, it's an understandable stance from Barkley, as running out of under-center formations should help him. As Fowler notes, "That way, he can see the linebackers and safeties more clearly and set up big gains."

Being able to generate explosive runs was something the Eagles were missing in 2025, and if the under-center formations can help him run off some big gains, then the Eagles should be all about making that change.

Fortunately, Mannion is implementing more under-center plays for this Eagles offense, and hopefully, that means there are big plays awaiting Barkley this upcoming season.

title: Ravens CB Nate Wiggins carted off practice field
description: The third-year cornerback appeared to injure his left leg after a 1-on-1 matchup with rookie wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane.
fullText:
Baltimore Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins was carted off the practice field at training camp on Tuesday after appearing to injure his left leg.

Wiggins went down after a 1-on-1 rep against rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane. Both players were sprinting down the left sideline for a deep pass from Lamar Jackson with Wiggins going to the ground after the ball fell incomplete. He looked to be in considerable pain as team trainers rushed over with the cart following shortly after. He could not put much, if any, weight on his left leg as he went inside the Ravens' facility.

Head coach Jesse Minter did not offer any details regarding the nature or severity of the injury after practice, but expressed "optimism" regarding Wiggins and "a lot of confidence" in the rest of the team's cornerback room.

Wiggins, 22, revealed this offseason that he did not feel 100% during his first two NFL seasons. The 2024 first-round pick underwent groin surgery a few months ago and said last week that he was "feeling the best I have ever felt."

This is a breaking story that will be updated with more information.

title: La Liga defender’s agent confirms Barcelona interest: ‘It is true’
description: FC Barcelona remain attentive to the centre-back market following Ronald Araujo’s departure on loan to Liverpool. The club’s sporting department continues to monitor several options in case an att...
fullText:
FC Barcelona remain attentive to the centre-back market following Ronald Araujo's departure on loan to Liverpool.

The club's sporting department continues to monitor several options in case an attractive opportunity emerges to strengthen the defense, although its priorities remain clear: Rodri and a new striker.

Against that backdrop, Real Betis defender Natan's name has gained momentum as a potential target for the La Liga champions.

Now, Natan's representative, Andre Cury, has confirmed that Barcelona have already contacted Real Betis to find out about the Brazilian defender's situation.

Cury told the Arab outlet Erem News that the Blaugrana have shown an interest in the Betis defender, although he stressed that the contacts have not yet resulted in a formal offer.

Barcelona eyeing Natan. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

"It is true that Barcelona are interested in signing Natan, but we have not received any official offer yet," the representative said, as quoted by SPORT.

The Brazilian agent also explained that the initial approach has taken place directly between the two clubs, with Barcelona yet to contact Natan's representatives.

"Barcelona haven't spoken to me, but they have spoken to the Real Betis board about their interest in signing Natan this summer. If Betis receive a good offer, I think he could leave," Cury added.

The interest therefore seems genuine, but the operation remains at an early stage.

Barcelona have asked about the conditions of a potential deal and sounded out Real Betis, but there is no active negotiation or formal offer on the table.

Not a priority. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Araujo's departure has reduced Flick's options in central defence, but the German coach has not demanded an urgent signing for the position.

Barcelona believe they already have solutions within the squad, particularly through La Masia.

One of the alternatives most highly regarded by the coaching staff is Alvaro Cortes. The young centre-back has gained prominence during preseason and Flick is counting on him to complete the first-team defensive rotation this season.

That option would allow Barça to fill the gap left by Araujo without committing resources to a position that is not currently among the market priorities.

For that reason, Natan remains a possibility that Barcelona are monitoring rather than a deal that is actively being negotiated. The interest is real, but the operation is still a long way from being underway.

title: Newcastle Rekindles Interest in Disgruntled Manchester City Forward After Bruno Exit
description: Newcastle United has significant work still to do before the transfer window closes after a summer in which the club has lost several established stars and undergone a managerial change, with Matthias Jaissle now overseeing the rebuild at St. James’ Park following Eddie Howe’s exit. One familiar transfer target has now resurfaced as a potential […]
fullText:
Newcastle United has significant work still to do before the transfer window closes after a summer in which the club has lost several established stars and undergone a managerial change, with Matthias Jaissle now overseeing the rebuild at St. James' Park following Eddie Howe's exit.

One familiar transfer target has now resurfaced as a potential attacking addition for the Magpies.

CaughtOffside's Mark Brus reports that Newcastle has rekindled its interest in Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush, with industry figures believing the Magpies could be particularly well positioned to meet City's valuation after the Bruno sale was confirmed on Saturday.

"Newcastle know they need to do some serious business up front," a source told Brus. "Their forward signings last summer haven't done it, there are already serious doubts about Nick Woltemade's future, and Marmoush is someone they've got high up on their list."

Newcastle's renewed interest comes after the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno generated significant transfer income, with those three sales alone totaling up to £250 million. According to CaughtOffside, that strong financial position could give the Magpies an advantage if their interest develops into an actual bid.

"He won't come cheap, but Newcastle are under pressure to make a splash like that now, after recouping so much from player sales," the source told Brus. "There hasn't been an approach yet, but it's one to keep an eye on, for sure."

According to CaughtOffside, Manchester City values Marmoush at approximately €60 million to €65 million (£52.2 million to £56.5 million), with "respected figures in the industry" believing Newcastle could be best placed to afford that asking price.

The 27-year-old's situation is worth monitoring because City is not actively pushing him out. While Brus reports that the Cityzens would be comfortable retaining Marmoush for squad depth, he adds that intermediaries familiar with Marmoush's situation in Manchester and Enzo Maresca's plans expect City to consider doing business if the club's valuation is met.

Newcastle, however, would also face stiff competition. Tottenham and Barcelona reportedly remain interested in Marmoush, but the good news is neither appears to have made him its immediate priority as things stand. That said, Spurs held informal contacts with the player and club, but Tottenham seems to be focused on other targets, according to CaughtOffside.

fullText:
PGA Tour star Tommy Fleetwood was impressed by one former NFL player's golf swing on the Pat McAfee show.

Athletes often become golf lovers after retiring, and former New England Patriots cornerback Darius Butler is no different.

Butler has become an avid golfer since his NFL retirement, and he did not waste the opportunity to show Fleetwood his swing.

Darius Butler explained to Tommy Fleetwood on the Pat McAfee show that he is struggling to improve his golf game.

"I've kind of plateaued at about mid-80s, and I can't get over that hump," he told Fleetwood.

A typical round in the mid-80s suggests that Butler is roughly a 10-handicap who wants to reach single figures.

After watching Butler's swing through the video call, Fleetwood joked: "There's no helping it. We don't have enough time for the show."

However, the world number six then admitted he was very impressed and could not believe Butler does not shoot lower scores.

"You look great," Fleetwood added. "There's no way you're only shooting in the mid-80s. I'm not having that. I'm not playing you for money."

Butler then revealed that "getting off the tee" is his biggest weakness. "If I'm off the tee, I'm good."

title: How Stefon Diggs will change Washington Commanders offense this season
description: What does Stefon Diggs, Jayden Daniels’ newest weapon,bring to David Blough’s offense?
fullText:
Fans were banging the drum for additional help at wide receiver all offseason. They received it in the form of Maryland native Stefon Diggs. The team had reportedly been in talks with the free agent for some time and reached a favorable agreement early enough to integrate Diggs in time for the regular season opener.

So, how will Diggs change the Commanders offense? Let's put culture concerns aside and take a look at his fit within new coordinator David Blough's proposed scheme.

Diggs was very efficient in limited snaps last year. He played 55% of the New England Patriots offensive snaps but was first in catch rate and second in success rate in the entire league, while his 75% contested catch rate was the second-highest of his career. His productivity is proven over 11 seasons, which includes four consecutive Pro Bowl appearances and 11,504 receiving yards. Not only does that rank 38th all-time, but it's also sixth among active players. Diggs has recorded seven 1,000-yard seasons in his career, including a 2020 campaign where he paced the league with 1,535 yards.

Provided by Pro-Football-Reference.com: View Original Table
Generated 8/10/2026.

Additionally, Diggs has the versatility David Blough looks for in his offense with the ability to play X, Z, or the slot role. Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels described his versatility as a "9 out of 10," and he used Stefon in an approximately 50/50 mix between in the slot and as an outside receiver.

Diggs wins with refined route running, tempo, and elite footwork. While the 32-year-old wide receiver has lost a step in terms of pure speed, he still has the ability to get the better of cornerbacks on the outside. That said, he thrives in the short to intermediate parts of the field and should be expected to run plenty of deep overs, high crossers and dig routes. Diggs is particularly adept at adjusting his routes to capitalize on space versus both man and zone coverage, with David Blough stating, "In just a couple days – he had four catches the other day, at least 2-3 today – the ball finds him because he finds space."

Big fan of the Stefon Diggs tape from last year. He clearly still has the juice and can separate at a high level. Here's a few of my favorites pic.twitter.com/vNC7kxj6Em

Yesterday, I broke down what new Commanders WR Stefon Diggs brings to Washington. Today, I'm looking at how he might fit in David Blough's new offense, with the flexibility to play Z or slot.

Full breakdown: https://t.co/NXzV8AAU9r pic.twitter.com/jKm4ez8ZOu

There is one more statistic that I did not mention before but would like to touch on here. Diggs ranked eighth in total receiving yards on motion plays last year. Keep in mind, he only played half of the Patriots total offensive snaps, so the number shows how effective he can be was when used in motion concepts. Not coincidentally, Blough is expected to incorporate them heavily in his new offense. As Blough stated earlier in the offseason:

I want it to be creative, aggressive, and I want whenever the coach on the other side turns the film on, I want them to feel stressed for every time we have the ball in our hands, of shifts, motions, breaking the huddle with urgency, getting us into premier plays."

This is how Diggs will alter Blough's offense. He won't change it conceptually but instead improve its effectiveness. Having another true threat opposite Terry McLaurin will allow Blough to stress the defense with motion and formation changes. If the veteran receivers line up on opposite sides, the defense must decide whether to shade safety help toward one boundary or the other. If Terry and Stefon align on the same side, Washington can stress and test communication through stacks and switch releases. Move either wide receiver into the slot; the defense has to reveal whether it will follow with a cornerback, pass the assignment to a nickel defender or change the coverage.

Washington can also use orbit or return motion to identify man coverage pre-snap. Forcing those decisions helps provide a clearer picture of the defense for quarterback Jayden Daniels before the snap and reduces the amount McLaurin needs to win in static alignments. Diggs represents that threat, and for those that have been following training camp, you can quickly see how Diggs differs from the players Washington already had in the wide receiver room.

Stefon Diggs looks GOOD!! That 18 ain’t bad either 👀#Commanders #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/skLLjntt66

Being "multiple" out of heavy personnel only works if the offensive play calling stays balanced out of these looks. The addition of Diggs will also allow the team to be effective with only two wide receivers. Along with Chig Okonkwo at tight end and a dual-threat running back, the defense must choose between a lighter coverage group or a heavier run-stopping option. If they go light, the offense can run the ball. If they go heavy, they can isolate a receiver against a linebacker or safety. Signing Diggs will allow Blough to keep both options credible and force the defense to honor them improving both the passing and rushing attack.

Just as importantly, Diggs gives Daniels another receiver he can trust, especially in hot reads and critical situations. Of Diggs' 85 catches last season, 51 of them resulted in first downs, for a 60% conversion rate. That falls in line with how Stefon has been for most of his career, as he has accounted for 561 first downs during his time in the league. Diggs also knows how to separate and win quickly, which has increased importance following the loss of Laremy Tunsil to a triceps injury.

Tunsil's absence will definitely be felt this season and may limit what Blough can do in multiple tight end sets and long-developing plays, but Adam Peters has already added another talent in Diggs that can elevate the Commanders offense and mitigate some of the loss this season.

title: Yankees At-Bat of the Week: George Lombard Jr. (8/8)
description: Lombard’s leadoff home run in the seventh inning against the Braves on Saturday turned out to be the game winner.
fullText:
I don't want to spill too much ink on the sorry state of the Yankees offense at the risk of sounding like a broken record. Instead, let's focus on the positives they have provided us in recent days, namely an improbable series win over the Braves. As much as the pitching largely carried the day, a certain young shortstop provided a handful of bright sparks on either side of the ball, and so George Lombard Jr. earns his first appearance on At-bat of the Week.

We join Lombard leading off the bottom of the seventh of the middle game against the Braves on Saturday. The Yankees are clinging to a 3-2 lead courtesy of a Spencer Jones RBI single in the second and RBI triple in the fifth, Austin Wells then driving him home with a double. Lombard enters this AB having struck out and drawn a walk against Chris Sale, the latter result requiring a pair of impressive, successful ABS challenges. However, Lombard now faces the hard-throwing righty reliever Victor Mederos, a very different look from the sidearming southpaw Sale.

Mederos starts Lombard with a first pitch sinker at 96 looking to tie the hitter up on the inner half.

This is a really good take from Lombard. The sinker looks like a strike on the upper ledge of the strike zone for much of its path toward home. It exits Mederos' hand aimed pretty centrally, yet Lombard is able to diagnose it immediately as a fastball and understands that the foot-and-a-half of arm side run will carry it all the way off the plate and out of the zone inside for a ball.

That was a pretty good pitch that Mederos just threw, so it makes sense that he sticks with the inside sinker as it's a pitch that can really eat up a hitter when buried in on the hands.

This is exactly why we don't bunt unless it is absolutely necessary. When you've got a reliever coming in and throwing upper-90s, a middle-middle sinker in a 1-0 count might be the best pitch you're gonna get to hit. Not only did Lombard miss a golden pitch to hit, but he lost his count leverage without making the pitcher work for it. Yes, I understand the third baseman was playing back and the Yankees are struggling for base runners at the moment, but Lombard was brought up to swing the bat (and for his glove) and bunting in this spot amounted to giving away a pitch.

Now that Mederos has shown Lombard a pair of fastballs that break toward him, he switches to a cutter breaking away from the batter, hoping he can get him to chase something off the plate outside should he mistakenly assume it is another sinker breaking in.

Mederos yanks this pitch way out of the zone, the pitch passing through the lefty batter's box and off the catcher's mitt to the backstop. It's one of the easier takes Lombard will get, though it was still informative for him to see a fastball that breaks in the opposite direction from the first two he saw.

After missing so wildly with that cutter, Mederos breaks out his third different fastball of the encounter, the four-seamer. His four-seamer breaks a little less down and a little less arm-side than his sinker, but the two pitch types otherwise aren't all that distinguishable from each other.

Mederos nails the outside edge with this 97 mph heater. He's partially able to catch Lombard looking by sequencing this pitch directly following a fastball that breaks glove-side, this pitch starting well off the plate away before tailing back into the zone, but mostly it's just a well-executed fastball that Lombard is more than justified to watch for a called strike.

Mederos now tries to leverage that called strike on the outside edge by sequencing a cutter that, as we mentioned, moves in the opposite lateral direction as his sinker and four-seamer. Lombard just watched a pitch that looked like a ball away end up as a called strike on the outside edge, so he effectively has to protect against anything that starts aimed away. This should make him susceptible to chasing a pitch that breaks glove-side.

Instead, Mederos grooves this cutter up and out over the plate. It doesn't have any of the cut of the first one he threw and flies straight as an arrow toward home. Lombard fires a beautiful swing lining this pitch into the seats in right for a leadoff home run to give the Yankees an invaluable late insurance run that they would need by the time the final out was recorded. I'll be honest, I did not realize Lombard had opposite field home run power, short porch or not. However, I love his approach, staying behind the baseball and allowing the velocity on the pitch to supply the power off the bat, knowing that with solid contact in the air, there's always a chance to leave the yard in right.

Without getting ahead of ourselves from a five-game sample, it is all the same assuring that Lombard has not looked overmatched facing big league pitching according to the eye test. We were always told that the defense was MLB-ready and indeed Lombard already looks way more rangy and self-assured at short than Anthony Volpe. However, I was not expecting him to have such an immediate impact with the bat. The power is certainly a welcome surprise, but it's his advanced pitch recognition and plate discipline that have really caught the eye and could be the keys to maintaining this form down the stretch.

title: On The Horizon: Cubs vs. Nationals series preview
description: The Cubs head to the nation’s capital for a three-game series.
fullText:
The Nationals were the Cubs' first regular season opponent this year, way back in March. The Nats took two of three at Wrigley Field.

Much has changed for both teams since then. The Cubs have solidified their claim on a postseason spot and could still win a division title. After playing over .500 for quite some time, the Nats had a selloff at the Trade Deadline.

For more on the Nationals, here's Sam Sallick, manager of our SB Nation Nationals site Federal Baseball.

The Nats are a very different team to the one that played the Cubs on Opening Day. Only two members of the bullpen remain and many fixtures of the lineup are now gone. Joey Wiemer, who dominated the Cubs to start the season, has now gone, with his rise and fall taking place over the course of six weeks.

However, the Nats remain on the outskirts of the playoff race. These last couple weeks have been a rollercoaster though. After beating the Diamondbacks in a series, they got within one game of a playoff spot and were over .500. Shortly after that, they hit a snag, losing seven in a row and selling at the deadline.

This past weekend though, the Nats got back into the fight by sweeping the Reds. The Nats lost the likes of Luis Garcia Jr., Curtis Mead and Foster Griffin at the deadline. However, a lot of the returns they received were made with the idea of helping the team in the near future.

The Nats bullpen has been a well publicized disaster, but with some new faces, they looked great against the Reds. Yovanny Cruz, Will Dion and Jake Bird all came over in deadline trades and have looked good in a Nats uniform. Nats POBO Paul Toboni has been searching for bullpen answers all season, but this is the best they have looked all year.

Usually, losing the NL leader in slugging would be a huge blow to the offense. However, rookie Abimelec Ortiz has looked very good stepping into Luis Garcia's shoes. Andres Chaparro has also stepped up making the first base platoon very dangerous.

There is one dangerous name the Cubs will avoid this week. James Wood is on the IL with a mild oblique strain. He is the most fearsome piece in this elite Nats offense. However, this offense is more than just Wood. CJ Abrams has also been tremendous and there are other hot bats such as Daylen Lile and the resurgent Keibert Ruiz.

On the pitching side, you are likely to see the debut of Jackson Kent, the Nats top left handed pitching prospect. He is a funky lefty with an average heater, a great changeup, solid breaking balls and good command. Kent is someone the Nats are very high on.

Right after the deadline, it looked like the Nats might have gone in a tailspin. However, they just got their first sweep since April and are riding high. It will be interesting to see how the surprising Nats matchup with a veteran laden Cubs team.

This is the first time the Cubs will play at Washington immediately after having played at Kansas City. Earlier this season, they went from Cleveland to Tampa and from Baltimore to Cincinnati for the first times. Next month, they will make their first trip from Miami to Milwaukee.

The Cubs have won two more games than they have lost at Washington, 35-33, since the former Montreal Expos relocated to the nation's capital in 2005. The Cubs also were 49-33 against two 19th Century NL teams in Washington, for a total record of 84-66.

Last year, the Cubs won two of three at Washington. They swept three in 2024. They last were swept at Nationals Park in 2019. They split four games in 2021, won two of three in 2022 and went 1-3 in 2023.

Tuesday: Shōta Imanaga, LHP (8-9, 3.60 ERA, 1.093 WHIP, 4.38 FIP) vs. Jake Irvin, RHP (2-5, 5.37 ERA, 1.290 WHIP, 4.73 FIP)

Wednesday: David Peterson, LHP (3-1, 4.03 ERA, 1.237 WHIP, 4.51 FIP in seven starts with Cubs; 6-7, 5.35 ERA, 1.500 WHIP, 4.08 FIP in 23 games overall) vs. Miles Mikolas, RHP (3-9, 5.89 ERA, 1.407 WHIP, 5.72 FIP)

Thursday: Kevin Gausman, RHP (1-0, 2.57 ERA, 0.714 WHIP, 4.23 FIP in one start with Cubs; 6-10, 4.29 ERA, 1.258 WHIP, 3.53 FIP in 24 starts overall) vs. Cade Cavalli, RHP (9-5, 3.57 ERA, 1.298 WHIP, 3.60 FIP)

Tuesday: 5:45 p.m. CT, Marquee Sports Network

Wednesday: 5:45 p.m. CT, Marquee Sports Network

Thursday: 3:05 p.m. CT, Marquee Sports Network

The Nats lead MLB in runs — but as noted by Sam Sallick above, two of the guys who helped lead them to that (Luis Garcia Jr. and Curtis Mead) have been traded and another (James Wood) is on the IL. The Nats have also allowed the third-most runs in MLB and the Cubs are second to them in runs scored.

All that adds up, I think, to a Cubs series win, two of three, and an outside chance of a sweep.

The Cubs return to Wrigley Field to host the St. Louis Cardinals in a three-game series beginning Friday afternoon.

title: Mike McCarthy shares key update on Steelers rookie Max Iheanachor
description: Mike McCarthy provided an update on first-round draft pick Max Iheanachor as the Pittsburgh Steelers prepare for their preseason opener.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are taking a cautious approach with first-round pick Max Iheanachor as the team prepares for its preseason opener.

According to media reports from Steelers beat writer Nick Farabaugh, head coach Mike McCarthy expects the rookie offensive tackle to sit out Thursday night's matchup against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium, though he remains on the verge of a full return to action.

Reporting on McCarthy's update, Farabaugh posted to X: "Mike McCarthy says Max Iheanachor is almost certainly OUT against the Packers on Thursday, but he's 'getting close' to being back fully."

Mike McCarthy says Max Iheanachor is almost certainly OUT against the Packers on Thursday, but he's 'getting close' to being back fully.

Iheanachor sustained an upper-body injury, specifically to his neck and shoulder area, during practice last week and was initially held out of full-contact team drills. While the developmental tackle out of Arizona State has made noticeable progress by returning to the practice field in full pads for limited individual work, the coaching staff is prioritizing long-term health and strength recovery before exposing him to live game reps.

Missing the preseason opener is an unfortunate bump in the road for the 21st overall draft pick, who had been generating significant momentum during the opening weeks of training camp in Latrobe.

Iheanachor's early performances in one-on-one padded drills showcased his impressive length and physical potential, fueling competition alongside veterans Broderick Jones and Dylan Cook for reps at right tackle.

Given McCarthy's cautious timeline, the Steelers appear inclined to preserve Iheanachor for the remaining preseason slate once he passes all final medical hurdles.

While fans will have to wait a little longer to see the rookie make his official NFL debut, McCarthy's encouraging diagnosis indicates that Iheanachor's absence will be brief as he works his way back into full team activities.

title: Duan Jansen, Marco’s twin brother, earns maiden South Africa call-up for Namibia tour
description: Duan Jansen, twin brother of Marco, has received his maiden South Africa call-up for the Namibia tour. The Proteas will play a T20I tri-series against Namibia and Zimbabwe before a historic three-match ODI series against Namibia. Bjorn Fortuin will captain the squad, while several domestic performers have earned opportunities to strengthen South Africa’s international depth.
fullText:
Duan Jansen, twin brother of South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen, has earned his maiden senior call-up and could make his international debut during South Africa's upcoming white-ball tour of Namibia.

The 15-member squad, led by experienced spinner Bjorn Fortuin, will play a T20I tri-series involving Namibia and Zimbabwe before taking on Namibia in a historic three-match ODI series.

The T20I tri-series will be played in Windhoek from August 28 to September 6, followed by three ODIs against Namibia from September 9 to 13. The ODI series will be the first bilateral 50-over contest between the two neighbouring countries.

Duan's selection comes after an impressive 2025/26 domestic season. He was named Division 1 One Day Cup Player of the Year and played a key role in helping the Titans win the title, scoring an unbeaten 61 in the final against the Lions.

Eathan Bosch is the other uncapped T20I player, while Connor Esterhuizen, Jordan Hermann and Nqobani Mokoena have received their first ODI call-ups.

"We've selected one squad for both series as we feel we have all departments well covered and it provides a great opportunity for players to build on their international caps. We saw glimpses of what Connor and Nqobani can offer during the T20I series against New Zealand earlier this year. It was unfortunate that Jordan picked up an injury in the opening match of that series, so we're looking forward to seeing him get another opportunity at this level."

Coach Shukri Conrad said using the same squad for both formats would give the players greater continuity and valuable international exposure. Nationally contracted players Dewald Brevis, Tony de Zorzi and Kwena Maphaka will provide additional experience.

"This tour has also opened the door for players who have performed domestically. Duan is one of those players. He is a quality all-rounder who has also shown great character for the Titans. Bjorn is an experienced player and proven leader who has successfully captained the Lions, and we have every confidence in his ability to lead this group. It is always exciting to play against our neighbouring countries, and the first-ever ODI series between South Africa and Namibia adds further significance, especially as we build towards next year's World Cup," he added.

South Africa are scheduled to leave Johannesburg for Windhoek on August 25.

title: How a roster loophole could solve Steelers' four-QB dilemma
description: By utilizing a practice squad loophole with veteran Mason Rudolph, the Pittsburgh Steelers can retain Will Howard and Drew Allar on the roster.
fullText:
As the Pittsburgh Steelers navigate a delicate quarterback puzzle behind starter Aaron Rodgers, head coach Mike McCarthy faces a classic 53-man roster crunch.

Carrying four quarterbacks: Rodgers, veteran Mason Rudolph, second-year passer Will Howard, and third-round rookie Drew Allar, is virtually unheard of in modern NFL roster construction. However, an intricate roster loophole involving Rudolph's status as a "vested veteran" could offer Pittsburgh an ideal strategic compromise to keep everyone.

Because Rudolph possesses at least four accrued NFL seasons, he is legally exempt from the league's waiver wire system if released. While non-vested young prospects like Howard or Allar would be exposed to waiver claims from 31 other teams, Rudolph immediately becomes an unrestricted free agent who can re-sign on his own terms.

During a recent segment on "PFT Live," NFL analyst Mike Florio broke down how Pittsburgh could exploit this procedural mechanism to protect its entire quarterback room:

"The veteran, the vested veteran gets cut, doesn't have to sign through waivers, hangs around, re-signs to the roster, signs to the practice squad. They could put Mason Rudolph on the practice squad, elevate him to the active roster, send him back down, do that a few weeks, and then do it all over again, release him from the roster," explained Florio.

Under NFL practice squad regulations, teams can elevate a veteran player up to three times per season without signing them to the active 53-man list. By executing a handshake agreement with Rudolph, Pittsburgh could temporarily release him at final roster cutdowns, stash him on the practice squad, and promote him on game days when needed.

This clever procedural maneuvering would allow the Steelers to retain their high-upside developmental assets on the 53-man roster while preserving Rudolph's essential veteran presence behind Rodgers without burning a valuable position spot. While reliant on mutual trust and personal flexibility, it provides Pittsburgh a unique mechanism to solve an otherwise difficult numbers game.

This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: How a roster loophole could solve Steelers' four-QB dilemma

title: Saints need 'controlled aggression' from rookie guard Jeremiah Wright
description: Jeremiah Wright is still the third-string right guard, but 'controlled aggression' and clean play 'down after down' can help him climb the depth chart
fullText:
The New Orleans Saints might not have planned to rely heavily on Jeremiah Wright immediately. However, as training camp has progressed, injuries appear to be accelerating the rookie right guard's development. The Saints lost veteran lineman Dillon Radunz for the season after he suffered a torn ACL in practice. The injury removed an experienced and versatile reserve from the equation, creating an opportunity for Wright to earn meaningful snaps earlier than initially anticipated. The Saints selected the 6-foot-5, 331-pound Wright with pick No. 132 overall in April's draft. After missing a couple of practices himself, the former Auburn Tigers starter returned to the field on Tuesday and immediately caught head coach Kellen Moore's attention.

"Good player, physical player," Moore Moore told local reporters after practice on Tuesday. "I thought today, getting back in there, he showed the same physicality that he showed early in camp."

Moore expects Wright to receive extensive work during the Saints' upcoming joint practices and preseason games. Those reps will give the coaching staff a better indication of whether he's prepared to contribute once the regular season begins: "I love what he's doing right now, and he's playing some really good football."

Wright said he'll be prepared whenever that opportunity arrives. He pointed to his work with veteran guard David Edwards as an important part of refining his technique and learning how to use his natural power.

"Sometimes I'm an aggressive guy, so I can overdo it," Wright said on Tuesday. "But with him, it's just being under control — controlled aggression — and getting to my spot."

The physical tools aren't in question for Wright. Moore said the next step will be playing clean, consistent football "down after down," particularly as the speed and intricacies of NFL defenses increase.

Wright isn't guaranteed an immediate role, but the Saints' circumstances have moved his development into the spotlight. With Radunz unavailable and several important evaluation periods approaching, the Saints could need their fourth-round pick to be ready sooner than expected.

This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Saints need 'controlled aggression' from rookie guard Jeremiah Wright

title: Anna Huang, 17, rises up in Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings

fullText:
With so much attention on youth the last few weeks, don't overlook Anna Huang. She made it through Ladies European Tour qualifying at age 16, and the Canadian has not missed a beat.

Huang was caught in a duel with Charley Hull on Sunday in the PIF London and held her nerve. Hull four-putted for double bogey on the 17th hole and Huang closed with an eagle to win by two. The 17-year-old now has four LET victories in the last 11 months.
