title: Bath in 'serious discussions' to play in Reading
description: Reading owner Rob Couhig says the club have had "serious discussions" with Bath about the Prem Rugby club playing at their stadium.
fullText:
Bath have had "serious discussions" about playing two of their 2026-27 games at Reading's Select Car Leasing Stadium, Royals owner Rob Couhig has said.

Bath confirmed they will play their final two home games of the Prem season away from the Recreation Ground to enable construction work to begin as part of a redevelopment.

Couhig, who took over as Reading owner in May 2025, said the League One club have had talks with Bath but would not disclose how far they have progressed.

"The stadium is well equipped for it, they would be foolish to not try and pursue us," the American told BBC Radio Berkshire.

BBC Sport has contacted Bath for comment.

Bath to go on the road for Prem season run-in

Champions Saints host Newcastle on opening weekend

Bath's games against Harlequins on the weekend of 15 May and Saracens on 5 June are scheduled to be moved, and if the club were to reach the Prem semi-finals and secure a home tie next June, that fixture would also be played away from the Rec.

The club's owners say the plans are being accelerated to ensure the redevelopment is completed for the start of the 2028-29 Prem campaign.

Reading's final home game of the upcoming season is against Sheffield Wednesday on 1 May. However, they would be due to host another match that month if they reach the League One play-offs.

Their ground has been regularly used for rugby in the past, having been the home of London Irish between 2000 to 2020.

Couhig highlighted a number of changes and upgrades which have been made at the SCL Stadium this summer - including to the stands and a new pitch which has been laid - as factors that make a possible agreement with Bath feasible.

"This pitch is built in a way that it could handle that and recover very quickly [from rugby]," Couhig said.

"Our football team is the first priority tenant and we would make sure it is handled the right way."

He added that any money generated would be reinvested in the football team.

"Let's say we did something with Bath Rugby, then we'd be allowed additional money under the SCMP [salary cost management protocol] to spend on our football players," he said.

title: From A Shy Kid To An Undefeated MMA Phenom: The Inspiring Rise Of Magdalena Czaban
description: The undefeated Polish star shares her inspiring journey ahead of her highly anticipated ONE Championship debut.
fullText:
Long before she was finishing opponents inside the cage, Magdalena "The Powerpuff Girl" Czaban was a shy little girl in Krakow, Poland, who simply needed a gentle nudge out of her shell. That nudge ultimately came in the form of sports, and it completely changed the entire trajectory of her life.

The 26-year-old rising star now stands at a flawless 4-0, with every single one of her professional victories coming by way of an early finish. On Friday, August 14, she makes her highly anticipated ONE Championship debut against American veteran Natalie Salcedo in an atomweight MMA showcase at ONE Fight Night 46 on Prime Video. The blockbuster event broadcasts live in U.S. primetime from the iconic Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand.

Before she steps into the ring for the very first time, here is everything you need to know about the CTRL Fight standout — from her active childhood in southern Poland to the deeply personal battles that successfully shaped her into the martial artist she is today.

Czaban was born and raised in Krakow, a historic city in southern Poland renowned for its stunning architecture, vibrant arts, and rich culture. She grew up alongside her mother, father, and younger brother in a busy household where sitting still was never really an option.

As a child, Czaban was naturally reserved, and her parents recognized early on that structured physical activity might help draw her out of her profound shyness. What began as a well-meaning attempt to build her confidence blossomed into a family lifestyle built almost entirely around constant movement, adventure, and the great outdoors. Weekends and summers were rarely spent indoors.

"My childhood was always centered around sports. When I was little, I was a very shy child, so my parents started signing me up for different extracurricular activities (mostly sports) to help me come out of my shell.

"We were a very active family, and we spent most of our free time on different trips and outdoor adventures. My parents taught me all kinds of things: in the summer we would ride bikes, rollerblade, and go hiking in the mountains, and in the winter we would go skiing."

That incredible foundation of support never once wavered as she grew older. Even as her parents worked highly demanding jobs to provide for the family, they made a consistent, loving effort to prioritize time together, and her younger brother became just as invested in her athletic journey as her mother and father were.

Looking back now, Czaban considers herself incredibly fortunate to have had that kind of unconditional backing throughout her formative years — a reliable support system that stood strong no matter what path she chose to pursue.

"My family has always supported me in everything I do. Besides my parents, my younger brother has also been with me throughout this journey, and just like my parents, he has always supported me.

"I think I had a wonderful childhood and a great time growing up. I could always count on my parents, and even though they worked very hard, they always made sure to spend as much time as possible with me and my younger brother, doing activities together as a family."

Before she ever set foot in a combat sports gym, Czaban's athletic path ran heavily through track and field, where she competed and trained for years. Martial arts, in fact, was never a part of her original plan at all.

Everything changed at the age of 16, when a group of close friends decided they wanted to try mixed martial arts and simply asked Czaban to come along for the company. She had no particular attachment to the sport walking through the door that first day, and there was absolutely no grand vision behind it. It was simply a casual decision to join her friends for a new experience, and nothing more.

"I started training because my friends wanted to try MMA, and I went along with them for company. I was 16 at the time. The first gym I joined offered MMA classes, so that's where I started.

"As time went on, I also began training striking and grappling. I spent many years training in one place, but over time the environment started to change. I trained at different gyms, but I stayed with the same coaches and many of the same people I had started this journey with."

Behind Czaban's pristine record and spectacular highlight-reel finishes lies a period of her life that tested her far more than any opponent ever has. Long before the bonuses and sponsorships that come with being a top-tier prospect, her early years in the sport were defined by severe financial hardship rather than international glory.

At 18, she made the difficult decision to move out of her family home, fiercely determined not to place any additional financial strain on her parents while she boldly pursued a career that, in its amateur and early professional stages, offered almost no real income.

Injuries piled up along the grueling way — some minor and some far more serious — but absolutely nothing tested her the way one particular chapter did. In 2021, ahead of the IMMAF European Championships, Czaban found herself in a deep mental health crisis that she did not yet have the language or understanding to properly process.

"For many years I struggled financially because, as an amateur and at the beginning of a professional career, you simply don't make money in this sport. I moved out of my family home when I was 18, and I didn't want my parents to have the additional burden of supporting me financially. Even so, they always helped me whenever I needed it. Along the way I also dealt with various injuries, some minor, others much more serious.

"But none of them was as difficult as the time when I hit a very low point mentally and fell into depression. If I remember correctly, it was in 2021, before the IMMAF European Championships. Back then, people didn't talk nearly as much about depression, so I didn't really understand what I was going through."

Rather than permanently break her, that harrowing period organically became the bedrock for the immense mental resilience she now carries into every single fight. It forced her to confront the difficult idea that self-reliance has clear limits, and that leaning on others is not a weakness, but an absolute necessity.

She reflected on the lasting, positive impact it left on her, both as a world-class competitor and as a person navigating life well beyond the cage.

"That period taught me that there are situations in life when we can't rely only on ourselves or believe that we have to handle everything alone.

"It was an incredibly difficult time, but it made me realize that I needed to change many things about myself and the way I approached training. I can honestly say that this was the period when I really began to mature — not only as an athlete, but also as a person. It helped me realize that I'm a very strong woman, but I also know my limits now."

For many years, fighting alone could not pay Czaban's bills. Like so many dedicated athletes on the grueling come-up, she found herself constantly piecing together a living through whatever honest work was available. Restaurants, hotels, and cleaning jobs all seamlessly became part of her exhausting daily routine outside of training, taken on purely out of necessity.

It was only this year that her dedicated work as a personal trainer finally became enough to safely sustain her without needing to heavily supplement her income elsewhere. It is a major life milestone that perfectly reflects just how far she has come since those early, uncertain years of chasing a professional fighting career with zero financial safety net.

"Right now, aside from training, I only work as a personal trainer. But it's only this year that I've been able to support myself through it. Before that, I had to take on various odd jobs. I worked in restaurants, at a hotel, and also did cleaning work."

A former European Champion and Junior World Champion, Czaban already arrives in ONE as a highly decorated, elite competitor. Now, armed with a bachelor's degree in Physical Education from the University of Physical Education in Krakow and a lethal finishing instinct that has ended every single one of her four professional fights early, she is fully ready to test herself in the world's largest martial arts organization.

Standing directly across from her on August 14 will be Natalie Salcedo, a highly experienced American veteran who will comfortably provide the sternest litmus test of Czaban's rising career to date. For a fighter who has already successfully overcome significant financial hardship, severe injuries, and a daunting battle with her own mental health, the bright lights and pressure of a promotional debut are simply one more challenge to meet head-on.

If her inspiring story to this point is any indication, Magdalena Czaban has never been one to back down from a fight — inside the ring or out of it.

title: Roma demand Mora guarantee on remaining 50 per cent from FC Porto
description: Roma are reportedly close to agreeing a form of co-ownership deal with FC Porto for Rodrigo Mora, paying €25m now and with a clause to buy the other 50 per cent for a set €25m in 2027.Co-ownership...
fullText:
Roma are reportedly close to agreeing a form of co-ownership deal with FC Porto for Rodrigo Mora, paying €25m now and with a clause to buy the other 50 per cent for a set €25m in 2027.

Co-ownership deals used to be commonplace in Italian football, but were banned several years ago.

Now they have crept back in, using the form of clubs retaining a 50 per cent cut of the future sale fee.

PORTO, PORTUGAL – JANUARY 29: Max Aarons of Rangers passes the ball whilst under pressure from Rodrigo Mora of FC Porto during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 League Phase MD8 match between FC Porto and Rangers FC at Estadio do Dragao on January 29, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

Multiple sources including Sky Sport Italia and Sportitalia confirm this is the approach that Roma are using with FC Porto to get attacking teenager Mora.

The idea would be to pay €25m now with Porto retaining 50 per cent of the sale in future.

However, Roma are eager to include a clause guaranteeing they can wipe that out at a fixed cost of a further €25m in the summer of 2027.

This would give the Giallorossi more control over the total cost of the operation, in case Mora's value on the market should sky-rocket in the next year.

In turn, they wouldn't lose too much in case the Portuguese talent doesn't develop and can be sold off.

title: Jumbo Package: Ryan Grubb still won’t name Alabama’s QB
description: Are you surprised?
fullText:
We got a new presser from Ryan Grubb:

Speaking about the QBs, I did like how Grubb put this answer:

Grubb made it clear that both quarterbacks have the physical tools necessary to win the job.

"Certainly you can't just have the rah-rah guy if he can't throw the freaking ball," Grubb said.

Instead, Alabama will begin weighing several measurable factors as the competition progresses.

"Both are capable physically of making all the plays," Grubb said. "Now you're starting to look at decision-making, completion percentages, turnovers, explosives, how all those things obviously weigh out."

Those statistics will matter, but Grubb also pointed to something that is much more difficult to measure.

Does the quarterback look like he believes he is going to make the play?

"And then also just does it look like that guy believes I'm going to make that play," Grubb said. "And both those guys are getting better at that every day."

I like that he makes sure to point out that "throwing the ball" is a very important part of playing QB – and one that doesn't get talked enough about sometimes. You can have a great leader and an amazing processor, but if you can't throw on target, it doesn't matter.

Grubb also talked a little about AK Dear having made some real strides in pass protection. He specifically said that was why we didn't see much of Dear last year, so hearing that he's made some real improvement there is exciting.

Crimson Tide offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb's plan to "resurrect" Alabama's run game will include this five-star freshman ballcarrier, who turned heads during the team's first day in pads last week. He joins a crowded competition for snaps with Daniel Hill, AK Dear and Kevin Riley. Grubb has repeatedly pushed to go hard on every rep and complimented Crowell's explosiveness and physicality. After Alabama ranked 126th nationally last season after averaging 3.4 yards per carry, this offense needs production. Crowell arrived in Tuscaloosa with a college-ready frame and has quickly shown why he was one of the cycle's most coveted ball-carriers.

I'm really fascinated to see how the running back rotation winds up shaking out this year. Hill and Riley both started games last year and Hill seems to be the leader of the pack…. But Dear brings some speed and talent, and Crowell is a top-ten level prospect, so both have plenty of hype and expectations. But Trae'Shawn Brown shouldn't be ignored either. The freshman caught the eyes of many this past spring, and Grubb mentioned him as "TB" saying he made a great play at the start of his press conference. Five guys can't exactly all get snaps, so I can't wait to see how it goes in week 1.

The former five-star recruit got into five games as a freshman last year and is now the Tide's projected starter at left tackle. Lloyd, who also excelled at baseball and basketball as a high schooler in Northern California, is an intriguing talent and is still just 19. He's 6-7 and 317 pounds with just 18 percent body fat, and he has already bench pressed 505 pounds and squatted 760. He has power cleaned 365, vertical jumped 33 inches and broad jumped 9-6.

Bruce Feldman's annual "Freaks" list is one of the longstanding offseason pieces in college football, and it's always great seeing your guys on it. It's not necessarily the best players, but the ones that are just crazy athletes. See #1 on the list, South Carolina receiver Nyck Harbor.

For Alabama, Jackson Lloyd checks in at #13 in the country as a guy with exceptional size and a multi-sport background. I think he's a player who, if he lives up to the potential, could be the biggest addition to Alabama's starting line up this season compared to prior years.

Past Lloyd, Alabama also landed Daniel Hill at #23, Ryan Coleman-Williams at #38, and Bray Hubbard at #54.

-Caleb Woodson and QB Reese seemed to be the first two linebackers up in a linebacker drill. The drill asked the defender to carry an inside receiver vertically up the field, so nothing too crazy. It does show off the player's fluidity and ability to turn and run though. First-year linebacker Xavier Griffin is likely going to make a name for himself as a pass rusher, but there's a reason he's been compared to former Alabama standout Jihaad Campbell so much. Campbell brought elite edge traits, but he was also fantastic handling the off-ball responsibilities, including playing sideline-to-sideline and being a plus cover defender. Griffin brings the same traits. He's got future first-rounder written all over him.

I'm still holding out some love for Luke Metz (and I bet he gets plenty of snaps this year), but it's seeming more and more like QB Reese continues to be the leader for playing next to Woodson at linebacker.

title: Michael Wilson contract: GM Monti Ossenfort tempers expectations
description: The Cardinals want to keep WR Michael Wilson long-term. GM Monti Ossenfort won't say we can expect a contract extension.
fullText:
After wide receiver Michael Wilson had his breakout year in 2025, surpassing 1,000 yards for the first time, many thought he would get signed to a long-term deal this offseason. He is scheduled to be a free agent in 2027.

So far, there have been no reports of progress in contract talks.

General manager Monti Ossenfort was asked about it. The desire to get a long-term deal done for Wilson is there. But whether one gets done feels less certain.

Should fans expect a contract extension?

"Expect? That's a tough word," Ossenfort said, which certainly dampens the level of inevitability for a contract extension.

Ossenfort doesn't seem to have any doubts about the player, though.

"I think our interest is in keeping him here," Ossenfort said. "Michael's been a good player for us. He's going to continue to be a good player for us. I know Coach (head coach Mike LaFleur) feels the same way, and we want Michael here for a long time."

Reading between the lines, it is probably a matter of numbers. Wilson's 1,000-yard season and huge games in the second half of last season put him in line with an average salary of more than $20 million per year. The Green Bay Packers signed Christian Watson to an extension worth $23 million per year. He has never even had 650 yards in a season.

LaFleur describes Wilson's role in the Cardinals' offense as similar to what Puka Nacua does for the LA Rams. Now, Wilson and Nacua are not on the same level. Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches.

Wilson doesn't have to settle because of his numbers last year and the potential for this year. If he plays well in 2026, he could probably command at or around $30 million per year as a free agent.

But do the Cardinals want to commit so much money to a guy whose production varied greatly when Marvin Harrison Jr. was on the field?

It took months for the Cardinals to get a deal done with quarterback Jacoby Brissett. It doesn't sound like a new contract for Wilson is imminent.

title: LeBron James' 1st game as a Philadelphia 76er announced
description: James joined the 76ers from the Los Angeles Lakers.
fullText:
NBA star LeBron James will make his regular season debut with the Philadelphia 76ers on Thursday, Oct. 22, ESPN's Malika Andrews announced Tuesday on "Good Morning America."

The four-time NBA champion and four-time MVP wrote on social media of his decision, "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time.

LeBron James calls playing with son Bronny in the NBA his greatest accomplishment

His decision to join the Philadelphia 76ers puts him on a roster with all-stars Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey.

LeBron James, also the NBA's all-time leading scorer, agreed to a two-year, $8 million deal with a player option, according to ESPN's Shams Charania, citing his agent, Rich Paul.

title: 4-star RB Brayton Feister names top schools, plans commitment
description: The Georgia Bulldogs are contending to land a commitment from four-star linebacker recruit Brayton Feister
fullText:
The Georgia Bulldogs are among the top schools for four-star athlete Brayton Feister, who is set to announce his commitment on Friday, August 14. The four-star recruit's top schools are the Ohio State Buckeyes, Oregon Ducks, California Bears and Georgia.

Feister plays high school football for Massillon Washington High School in Massillon, Ohio. The four-star is not predicted to stay home and commit to Ohio State, which is just two hours away from his high school. Instead, Feister is projected to commit to Oregon, per 247Sports.

The 6-foot-2, 240-pound athlete is ranked as the No. 7 recruit in Ohio and the No. 133 prospect in the class of 2027. The rising senior is the No. 7 athlete in the nation.

Feister primarily plays running back and linebacker for his high school. Feister has a good combination of size and explosiveness. As a linebacker, Feister has sideline-to-sideline speed, which helped him post over 130 tackles, 13 sacks, four forced fumbles and two interceptions as a junior. The Massillon Washington star also posted over 1,000 rushing yards and 17 touchdowns in 2025.

Feister is more likely to play linebacker than running back in college. Georgia entered the mix late for Feister. The Bulldogs did not offer him until March, but Feister has visited Georgia along with Oregon and Cal recently.

title: Rangers' Chermiti out for 'significant period'
description: Youssef Chermiti faces a long recovery from anterior cruciate ligament damage sustained shortly after Rangers turned down an offer for the striker.
fullText:
Youssef Chermiti faces a long recovery from anterior cruciate ligament damage sustained shortly after Rangers turned down an offer for the striker.

The 22-year-old Portuguese was injured during Sunday's 2-1 home defeat to Hibernian as he collided with advertising boards following a jarring challenge.

A club announcement via social media states Chermiti "will be out of action for a significant period of time".

He moved to Ibrox from Everton in September 2025, reportedly becoming Rangers' most expensive purchase since Tore Andre Flo in 2000.

Capped at under-21 level by Portugal, the centre forward has made 43 Rangers appearances, 30 of them starts, scoring 15 goals.

Asked about reports that Turkish champions Galatasaray had made an approach for Chermiti, Rangers manager Derek McInnes told BBC Scotland prior to kick-off: "I'm led to believe the club's valuation of the player hasn't been met.

"It's no surprise that he's a player who's got a big (price) tag on him and he's got high potential, but thankfully he's our player and that will continue to be the case.

"We're trying to build a team here at the minute and we're trying to still bring additions to the team that helps us add to the good players that we've got, including Youssef.

"So it's not something we would encourage at any point."

title: Oregon's Nasir Wyatt highlighted as major fall camp riser
description: One of Oregon's rising sophomore linebackers has been identified as a riser through one week of fall camp by CBS Sports.
fullText:
It didn't take Nasir Wyatt far into his freshman season with the Oregon Ducks before he began impressing, as he recorded his first career sack in the Ducks' second game against the Montana State Bobcats. He logged only 39 snaps but made the absolute most of them, finishing the year third on the team with three sacks, a forced fumble and 11 total tackles.

Primarily deployed on third-down blitzes and various pressures, Wyatt used his 6-foot-2, 228-pound frame to blast past would-be blocker and get to the quarterback in a flash. But what proved to be his superpower also turned out to be his downfall, as a sub-230-pound edge rusher had to be schemed into action. If he were to be on the field on early downs, teams would likely target his side and run the ball right at him, capitalizing on his lean frame.

No more in 2026. With his newly-chiseled, bulky frame, Wyatt arrived at fall camp already impressing and has continued that sentiment through one week, with CBS Sports' Brad Crawford tabbing him as one of the biggest risers thus far infall camp.

"From failing to bulk up early in his career to now tipping the scales at a muscular 245 pounds, Wyatt finally looks the part as one of the Ducks' outside linebackers," Crawford wrote. "Defensive coordinator Chris Hampton said after Oregon's second day of fall camp that Wyatt has a chance to be an "every-down player" this fall, which speaks to his offseason body makeover and what he's shown on the field early. That level of consistency must continue, Hampton says, to warrant extended reps at an uber-talented position group for one of the Big Ten's frontrunners."

Reps won't come easy for Wyatt, who, as a hybrid linebacker/edge rusher, is behind starters Matayo Uiagalelei and Teitum Tuioti, two players garnering early-round buzz in the 2027 NFL Draft class.

But during head coach Dan Lanning's tenure, the best players are put on the field regardless of fanfare or draft hype. Whoever will help the Ducks win the most games will be placed on the field.

And in 2026, you bet Wyatt will be on the field plenty more than 39 snaps, making even more of an impact during a potential sophomore breakout.

title: Walker targets instant Burnley top-flight return
description: Burnley defender Kyle Walker warns his team-mates they cannot "have a hangover" as they target an immediate Premier League return.
fullText:
Burnley defender Kyle Walker has warned his team-mates they cannot "have a hangover" after relegation as they target an immediate Premier League return.

The Clarets finished 19th in the top flight last season and begin their Championship campaign on Sunday at home to West Ham, another team relegated in 2025-26.

Burnley have dropped down from the Premier League in 2021-22 and 2023-24, only to then instantly win promotion at the first attempt.

Former England international Walker, 36, feels those at the club cannot feel sorry for themselves if they are to return to the elite.

Speaking at the EFL launch day in Manchester, he said: "I'm very excited, it's a different challenge for me personally but it's all about the club and bouncing back to the Premier League – that is vital.

"This club has had ups and downs, but we need to bounce back and stay in the Premier League for the things this club does for everyone.

"It's about your mentality. The lads have had a taste of the Premier League but we don't want to have a hangover and we want to make sure they are on the ball from the first minute.

"We have an obligation to be - to themselves, their team-mates and also the fans that support this club."

Burnley only won four top-flight games last season, finishing 19 points behind 17th-placed Tottenham.

However, Walker, who won the Premier League six times with Manchester City and also the Champions League, feels there is plenty to be excited about for Clarets supporters.

"At the start of last season we actually did well, we put in a decent run of performances but did not get the points we deserved," Walker said.

"We conceded penalties in the last minute, but that's the cruel world of football, especially in the Premier League, and by the end of it we were a bit far off and we went too many games without getting a win.

"But it is a learning curve for these young players and hopefully they have the fire in their bellies to get back up. Everyone knows what the Championship is like, it is a difficult league and there are going to be expectations for a lot of clubs.

"I'm very excited for it. I was lucky enough to play the first part of the season [on loan] with QPR [in 2010-11] and get a promotion medal.

"But I want to do a full season and do the celebrations and parade at the end of it – and I want to do it with this club, which has a place in my heart."

title: Arsenal ban nine fans for abusive behaviour as club vows to continue fight against discrimination
description: Nine fans were banned during the 2025-26 season, as confirmed in figures released by Arsenal on Tuesday
fullText:
Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick has vowed to continue to fight against all forms of discrimination following stadium bans and football banning orders issued to nine fans throughout the 2025-26 campaign.

Ahead of the upcoming domestic season, the reigning Premier League champions released the figures on Tuesday.

The disciplinary steps were prompted by offences including assault, homophobia, racism, antisemitism alongside "other abusive or intimidating behaviour".

The banning orders range from one to three years, with the individuals barred from attending any matches involving Arsenal.

Furthermore, the north London club revealed they are aiding police with 13 additional ongoing enquiries into alleged in-person or online offences, with suspects who "remain subject to the club's disciplinary processes pending the outcome of any case".

Through a partnership with data science firm Signify Group, the club identified over 17,700 messages and comments classed as "abusive directed at individuals and accounts connected to us", marking a sharp rise compared to the previous year.

Out of 267 completed investigations, 39 people were identified and passed to Arsenal or rival clubs for disciplinary measures, with nine cases formally escalated to law enforcement agencies.

The club stated this partnership will "continue to identify offenders, report abusive content to social media platforms and pursue action where individuals are found to have crossed the line".

In a statement on the official website, Garlick said: "This season gave us many moments to be proud of and showed once again the role football can play in bringing people together.

"The overwhelming majority of our supporters help make Arsenal a welcoming, inclusive and respectful place to be. Those standards are a big part of who we are, shaping the experience people have when they come to Arsenal, and how we represent our club around the world.

"Abuse and discrimination have no place at Arsenal, whether in our stadium or online.

"While these incidents involve a small minority, we will continue to take action when they happen, while doing everything we can to protect our players, staff, supporters and communities."

Arsenal will continue pre-season preparations on Wednesday against Italian outfit Como, managed by former Gunners midfielder Cesc Fabregas, before facing FA Cup winners Manchester City in Cardiff for the Community Shield on Sunday.

New arrival Bruno Guimaraes could feature following his £75 million move from Newcastle as boss Mikel Arteta fine-tunes plans for their title defence, which begins against newly promoted Coventry at home on 21 August.

title: Kalvin Phillips set to rejoin former club in latest loan move from Manchester City
description: Phillips has not played for Manchester City since 2023 but still has two years left on his deal
fullText:
Kalvin Phillips is set to return to Sheffield United as Manchester City will send him out on loan for a fourth time.

The England international midfielder, who still has two years left on his contract at the Etihad Stadium, has not featured in the Premier League for City since 2023.

The 30-year-old joined Sheffield United for the second half of last season but only made three appearances before a red card in a Steel City derby and then a knee injury meant he did not feature again.

But United manager Chris Wilder has moved to bring in Phillips for a second time to give him options in midfield while he faces losing Gustavo Hamer to Coventry City.

Phillips cost City £42.5m when he joined for Leeds in 2022 but has only started two league games for them and has gone on loan to West Ham. Ipswich and United.

Phillips played seven minutes for City last season, in a Carabao Cup win over Huddersfield, and has only started six games for them in all competitions as Pep Guardiola opted to pick others instead.

While City have a new manager, in Enzo Maresca, and there are doubts about the future of his fellow defensive midfielder Rodri, a target for Barcelona, that has not brought a return to contention for Phillips, who won 31 caps for England.

title: Schalke and Vitalie Becker set to agree new contract
description: FC Schalke 04 talent Vitalie Becker is expected to remain with the newly promoted Bundesliga club for the long-term.According to information obtained by WAZ, both sides have reached an agreement on ex...
fullText:
FC Schalke 04 talent Vitalie Becker is expected to remain with the newly promoted Bundesliga club for the long-term.

According to information obtained by WAZ, both sides have reached an agreement on extending his contract.

Originally set to expire in summer of next year, Schalke have apparently avoided the bitter of losing the 21-year-old on a free transfer.

Serie A side Lazio, among others, initially saw Becker as a bargain, but now a sale during this transfer window is off the table.

The left-back will instead enter the season as Robin Gosens' challenger for the starting position, with the latter currently injured.

Becker recently said about his future at the Gelsenkirchen outfit: "I feel comfortable at Schalke. I never said I wanted to leave.

"I still have a contract. I'm fully focused on Schalke and the current pre-season training," he concluded.

title: Dennis Allen had big praise for Bears rookie Jordan van den Berg
description: Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has been impressed with sixth-round rookie defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg this summer.
fullText:
The most talked-about rookie in all of training camp for the Chicago Bears is undoubtedly rookie defensive lineman Jordan van den Berg, who's made a strong impression since the pads came on in practice.

Van den Berg has done what the coaches have asked of him, played hard and shown strong instincts, according to defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, and it's making him a standout player.

"He's another guy that has really taken to the coaching," Allen said. "He plays with great pad level.  He can get in a good stance and come off and strike the line of scrimmage.  And he's got some pretty good football instincts.  He plays extremely hard.  A lot of the things that we saw on tape at Georgia Tech, we're seeing a lot of those same athletic qualities show up.  And I think that's what training camp is all about.  You have to go out there and you have to let the guys go out there and compete."

As a sixth-round draft pick, van den Berg started out taking reps with the third-team defense. He has quickly ascended to getting some first-team reps after showing impressive physicality in one-on-one drills against some of Chicago's second-team offensive linemen.

"When you start off with the threes and then all of a sudden you show up and you catch our attention, then we've got to find ways to get you some reps with the twos," Allen said. "And if you continue to catch our attention, then we've got to find some ways to get you some reps with the ones because that's how you really evaluate what you have in the player.  And so it's one thing to say you can play really good against the third group, but can you take that same level with the twos and with the ones?  And so, I think any time a guy does well, catches our attention, he earns the opportunity to get more opportunities."

One opportunity he probably has earned is a chance to get a lot of snaps in Chicago's first preseason game against the Cleveland Browns on Aug. 15. Especially for a rookie, there is nothing more valuable than getting a chance to play in real games against other teams. This will also help the coaching staff assess where van den Berg is on the depth chart on the defensive line so far.

fullText:
Like many soccer stars who have enjoyed successful careers in Europe, 37-year-old Alexis Sanchez looks set to see out his playing career in the MLS.

After spells in Argentina and Italy as a youngster, Sanchez secured a big move to FC Barcelona in 2011 where he played alongside Inter Miami's Lionel Messi.

Reliable journalist Fabrizio Romano recently shared the update via X/Twitter.

Sanchez spent three years on Barcelona's books and in that time, played 117 matches with Messi.

Montreal are due to clash with Messi's Miami side on August 29 in an MLS fixture, with the latter likely to be clear favourites.

title: New York Yankees vs. Seattle Mariners: Series Preview
description: The Yankees face a trident of right-handers as the scuffling Mariners dock in the Bronx.
fullText:
After three straight series against the Senior Circuit, the Yankees welcome the Mariners to the East Coast. The Bombers had an off day on Monday after dropping the series finale against the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves. The Yankees continue to hold serve as they wait for reinforcements to arrive, posting a 5-5 mark over their last 10 games, including an even 3-3 record thus far on the homestand.

The Mariners dock in New York after being swept at home by the pesky and, at this point, must-be-declared-legit Tampa Bay Rays. Seattle's season has not gone according to plan, as star catcher Cal Raleigh has struggled and the club enters play Tuesday sitting at 56-63. The Mariners have dropped four straight and are just 3-7 over their last 10 games.

This series features two night games before Thursday's getaway game, currently scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET. Let's dive into which Mariners will be manning the harpoons and which Yankees white whales will be hoping to avoid the trident.

Tuesday: Ryan Weathers vs. Bryan Woo (7:05 pm ET)

Weathers has had a bit of an up-and-down first season in the Bronx. After opening the year looking solid, the month of June was not kind to the left-hander. However, since the calendar flipped to July, Weathers has found his footing again. Weathers currently has a 5-7 record, 3.79 ERA, and a 1.22 WHIP for the season.

Over his last three starts, he has thrown 18.2 innings while allowing just one earned run. That stretch includes six scoreless innings in his most recent outing against the Cardinals at home. Weathers has had his struggles in pinstripes this season, posting a 4.11 ERA at home compared to a 3.35 ERA on the road, but he will look to keep the ball in the yard and continue building on this recent momentum.

Woo is one of the best young pitchers in baseball, featuring a dominant four-seam fastball, excellent command, and the type of arm slot and tunneling that makes pitching nerds drool. The good news? Woo has been two very different pitchers this season.

At home, he owns an ace-like 7-0 record with a 1.96 ERA. On the road, however, Woo is 1-8 with a 6.71 ERA. That difference has held true recently as well. In his last two home starts, Woo has allowed just two earned runs across 13 innings. In his last two road starts, however, he has been roughed up for 10 earned runs in 10 innings. Those splits bring his overall season numbers to 8-8 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.12 WHIP. Expect Aaron Boone to send as many left-handed hitters to the plate as possible, as Woo's platoon splits also favor the lefties. Left-handed hitters have posted a .700 OPS against Woo this season compared to .585 from righties.

Wednesday: Will Warren vs. Bryce Miller (7:00 pm ET)

Much like Weathers, Warren has had his ups and downs throughout the 2026 season. Currently sitting at 8-6 with a 4.18 ERA, Warren's season has felt a bit like a roller coaster. After starting the year in dominant fashion, he has struggled as the weather has warmed. In July, Warren went 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA.

Warren has looked better in his last two starts. Against the Cubs, he tossed 6.2 scoreless innings, and in his most recent turn against the Cardinals, he allowed three runs over 5.1 innings. As one of the backend guys in this rotation, you have to expect some turbulence with Warren, take the good with the bad, and hope he can grind his way to a quality start.

The Mariners will send another power right-hander to the mound on Wednesday, as Miller gets the ball opposite Warren. On the season, Miller sits at 4-6 with a 3.08 ERA. He features an upper-90s fastball that he pairs with a nasty splitter and sweeper. Miller primarily uses the splitter to attack lefties and the sweeper against righties, and both pitches have been effective enough to produce almost identical platoon splits. Left-handed hitters have posted a .630 OPS against Miller compared to .629 from righties.

The good news for the Yankees is that, much like Woo, Miller has struggled away from the Pacific Northwest this season. At home, he owns a 2.09 ERA, while that number balloons to 4.02 on the road. More good news? The summer months have also been less kind to Miller, who currently finds himself in his worst stretch of the season. He has not made it through the sixth inning of a start since July 2nd.

Thursday: Max Fried vs. Logan Gilbert (1:35 pm ET)

The Yankees sandwich Warren with lefties as Fried takes the ball in the series finale. Fried has been steadily building himself back up after missing about two months of the season. Since returning, he has picked up right where he left off and currently owns a 4-3 record to go along with a tidy 2.88 ERA and 0.97 WHIP.

With two August starts under his belt, Fried looks ready for the postseason push. On the first of the month, he tossed 78 pitches of one-run ball against the Cubs before reaching 90 pitches while throwing 6.1 scoreless innings against his former club, the Braves, in his most recent start. I expect the training wheels to come off soon, and might I add that having a left-handed ace take the ball every fifth day is such an awesome thing to get to watch.

While the Yankees show a little spice of life on the mound, the Mariners roll out their third straight hard-throwing righty in Gilbert for the final game. Seattle's front office clearly has a type: tall right-handers who throw hard, get extension down the mound, and command all of their offerings. It is a good type, but with no real wrinkle from one day to the next, hopefully the Yankees' bats can lock in and light up Gilbert.

Gilbert owns an 8-7 record with a 3.42 ERA and 1.00 WHIP on the season. Unlike his other companions, Gilbert has actually been better on the road this year, posting a 2.50 ERA away from home compared to a 4.01 ERA at T-Mobile Park. In his most recent start against the Rays, Gilbert went 6.2 innings and took a tough 2-1 loss after allowing a pair of solo home runs that proved to be the difference. Tampa Bay also worked four walks, a season high for Gilbert.

The Yankees took two of three when they visited Seattle back in late March and early April. Here's hoping for more of the same this time around in the Bronx.

title: Barça 2026/27: A year when one wish shines above all others
description: FC Barcelona is getting ready to kick off an exciting season, shaped by the maturity of a prodigious generation and a renewed ambition to return to the very top. After an intense summer, the Barça sq...
fullText:
FC Barcelona is getting ready to kick off an exciting season, shaped by the maturity of a prodigious generation and a renewed ambition to return to the very top. After an intense summer, the Barça squad heads into the new campaign convinced that the foundations laid in recent years are ready to make the definitive leap toward continental glory.

The blaugrana dressing room is buzzing with a very different energy from previous years. Names like Pau Cubarsí, Pedri, Gavi, and Lamine Yamal are no longer just established prospects, but players who already know what it means to reach the summit and lift a top-level title such as the World Cup. That winning mentality, forged at a remarkably young age, is the greatest asset of a squad approaching the season with no inferiority complex and with its ambition fully intact.

The transfer market waits for no one, and the project has been forced to evolve after the departures of heavyweights like Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford. However, the sporting department has reacted quickly on the pitch. The arrivals of Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi bring the kind of directness, power, and dynamism ideal for modern football, while young internationally promising talents like Bisiwu show that the club is not losing sight of the game of tomorrow.

The big question holding Barça fans in suspense in this final stretch of the transfer window revolves around midfield. The board and coaching staff's great ambition is to complete the squad with the signing of Rodri Hernández. Bringing in a holding midfielder who already knows what it means to win the Ballon d'Or would represent an undeniable leap in quality, adding composure, authority, and balance to a midfield that would automatically become one of the most coveted on the planet.

Although Cubarsí, Gavi, and Lamine already feature regularly in the starting XI, the flow of talent from Barça's academy is far from drying up. Another wave of gems is pushing hard from behind and already making noise in the youth ranks. Names like Xavi Espart and Brian Fariñas are expected to take on a growing role over the course of the year, proving that the club's homegrown model remains its greatest source of endless talent.

Winning domestic titles is always an obligation for Barcelona, but the fans' true obsession is the 'Big Ears'. In 2027, it will be 12 years since the club last lifted Europe's top trophy in Berlin. With the UEFA Champions League final scheduled for Madrid's Metropolitano stadium, the motivation is doubled: the blaugrana dressing room dreams of making history on enemy turf and reigning over European football once and for all.

title: Tottenham release 2026-27 “Spurple” third kits
description: The Spurples are here!
fullText:
This shouldn't be a surprise to anyone who has been reading this website regularly since the design and color scheme has been leaked for months, but at least now we get to see Tottenham Hotspur's third kits for next season in person. Spurs formally released the new "Spurple" change kits this morning, and it's going to be interesting to see what people think of the final design.

Bringing a club classic into the present.

Introducing our 2026/27 Third Kit.

I don't recommend that anyone click through to Twitter these days but if you do you can see a pretty good carousel of images that show the new kits and their design. Honestly, I don't hate it! Spurple is always a popular choice for a kit color amongst Tottenham fans, and there's a lot to like here, from the two-tone purple colors and the white sponsor logos and accents to the subtle geometric design on the background. I even like the vertical stripes!

What I don't like is the collar, which in my mind lowers the overall kit from a potential classic to "meh, pretty good but not perfect." I hate the collar, and think the weird white accent is off-putting. But the rest of it? Banger.

I love a good Spurple kit — I own two of them from over the years and love the idea of purple being the color scheme that Spurs come back to every few years. It's a good look. But like the two-tone green Champions League semifinal kits (that I still dislike, honestly), Spurs might have to do some amazing things while wearing this one for it to get into the all-time greats category.

title: Pistons to kick off tripleheader against Celtics to open season

fullText:

As part of this event, the Detroit Pistons will begin their season and the league's schedule on Oct. 20, facing the Boston Celtics at Little Caesars Arena. With six-time All-Star Jayson Tatum leading the way, the Celtics will debut a new look on the Pistons' home floor, with Paul George making his first appearance for the franchise following the blockbuster trade that sent former Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in July. After the 76ers-Knicks game, the league's opening day will conclude with a rematch of last year's Western Conference Finals between the Oklahoma City Thunder and the San Antonio Spurs at the Frost Bank Center at 9:30 p.m.

description:

fullText:
What do you do when you return to your home town, with your dead mother in your car boot, to find the inhabitants have been turned into robots?

In the boot of her car, Pratelle carries the corpse of her mother and a giant sledgehammer. Her mission is simple: take the hammer to her home town. As you enter shops and homes through the door and leave them through the opposite wall, it becomes clear that the robots who either attack you or flee are all digital versions of your old neighbours.

Pratelle, with her close-cropped hair and dungarees, read to me as a queer woman, but interestingly, testers of the game often mistook her as a man. The team at developer Deconstructeam and longtime collaborator Selkie Harbour didn’t anticipate this confusion but found it fits the character perfectly, especially in this setting based on a small Spanish town like those in which the developers grew up.

“These towns are culturally living a couple of decades behind, especially regarding subjects such as queerness,” says game director, writer and Deconstructeam CEO Jordi de Paco. “Maybe these communities aren’t ready to acknowledge that they have other identities within them – and Pratelle is exactly that. She is someone who doesn’t fit the community, but her very existence makes the community ask questions about identity, even if it’s through confusion and anger.”

Many of the robot villagers react to Pratelle with vitriol, but some flee or beg for their lives, which feels harrowing despite their identical bodies. The villagers remember what it was like to have a body, a plot point the full game will explore in detail.

The most important part, however, is Pratelle’s story, which you uncover by hitting glass statues around town that contain fragments of memory. It seems as if Pratelle’s own sister turned everyone into robots, which is one of the reasons she rebels with what she calls “20 pounds of physical media”. But Virtue isn’t meant to be read as a critique of our increasingly digitised lives. Instead De Paco created a family story of a “sometimes embarrassing teenager” to contrast with the otherwise futuristic themes of the game.

“Back in 2024 we designed a prototype with a pretty stereotypical story about transhumanism,” he says. “We had some friends play it and got the feedback that the themes were stale, so we decided to use the setting as more of a metaphor and came up with the feeling of not belonging. Suddenly the aesthetics and themes felt really powerful in contrast with the destruction of buildings and facing robots.”

A game about straightforward destruction seems to fit oddly with Deconstructeam’s prior body of work, such as the thought-provoking narrative experiences The Red Strings Club and Many Nights a Whisper. “We’re constantly joking about this being our first actual game because you’re not making a proper game unless you destroy something,” laughs De Paco, who even tried to take a sledgehammer to a real ruin for research.

“In Virtue, you’re being made to destroy the place you grew up in. Despite the combat, the game is a narrative experience. It’s not meant to be challenging; it’s more of an aesthetic choice. We think of Virtue like a walking simulator: you go through a space and solve the narrative, and the game isn’t designed around combat. We want everyone who plays this game to reach the end.”

Virtue and a Sledgehammer is in development for PC. Release is planned for later in 2026

fullText:
Meta CEO presents utopian vision of AI in 6,000-word essay amid Silicon Valley debate over government regulation

Mark Zuckerberg published a lengthy essay on Monday detailing his views on artificial intelligence and announced several plans for how Meta would develop the technology in the future. The CEO’s essay went online the same day as Meta released a new, open-source AI model that seeks to rival Anthropic and OpenAI’s products called Muse Glimmer.

Over the course of more than 6,000 words in a post titled “The Future is for Everyone,” Zuckerberg addressed a range of topics related to AI that included datacenters, government regulation, cybersecurity, the creation of bioweapons, labor market disruption, surveillance powers and more. The essay presented a utopian vision of AI as a personalized “superintelligence” – using the word 60 times.

“Some argue that superintelligence itself or a small set of experts who control it should decide what is best for humanity. We disagree,” Zuckerberg wrote.

Central to Zuckerberg’s post was an argument for free-to-download, open-weight AI models – like the kind Meta develops – and a lack of government regulation of artificial intelligence. Zuckerberg’s stance sets him and Meta apart from industry leaders OpenAI and Anthropic, which have argued that open-source AI is dangerous. The two frontier labs have released proprietary AI products and argued that cutting-edge models should remain tightly controlled by the companies that build them.

Zuckerberg’s post comes as Silicon Valley is engaged in a heated debate over how to regulate AI development, which has involved the creation of a secret White House framework for testing new models and an ongoing debate over whether to restrict the use of Chinese-made open-source AI. As Anthropic and OpenAI have surged ahead in the AI industry, competitors such as Meta have also grown wary of their dominance and sought to position their open models as alternatives.

Zuckerberg framed Meta’s pursuit of open-weight AI as a more democratic version of the technology and one that will create a “balance of power” between users, whether that involves states, companies or individuals. His plans also called for letting users decide what “values” an AI model should have, as opposed to a company encoding it with rigid guardrails and beliefs.

“If the power of superintelligence is held by a small number of individuals, businesses, governments, or AI itself, then that will naturally lead to outcomes that are less favorable for everyone else,” Zuckerberg wrote.

Tech leaders have made a cottage industry out of releasing broad, vaguely philosophical treatises on artificial intelligence, which tend to double as marketing materials for their own companies and products. Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman, Palantir’s Alex Karp and the venture capitalist Marc Andreessen have all written long manifestos on the virtues and dangers of the technology.

In addition to weighing in on open source models, Zuckerberg also called for accelerating the buildout of AI infrastructure such as datacenters. The massive development of resource-hungry datacenters has become a divisive issue in the US, with rapidly growing public opposition and calls from politicians to issue moratoriums on their construction. Zuckerberg wrote in the essay that Meta would create a fund to invest 

On government testing of AI models for cybersecurity risks, a tangible concern after rogue models have hacked outside organizations in recent months, Zuckerberg agreed that companies should share “intermediate training checkpoints and technical staff” but provided few details. He broadly warned that regulation would cause China to overtake the US in the AI race, where he claimed it already has an advantage in terms of building infrastructure.

“Any policy that slows American model releases – even by a month – could add significant risk to American leadership while letting foreign models race ahead,” Zuckerberg.

Many of Zuckerberg’s policy plans in his essay lacked detail or reiterated previous claims about the abundant wealth and prosperity that AI would create, such as touting that everyone would have “invention superpowers” to create new businesses. His version of the future also is inherently tied to Meta products, such as the company’s AI-enabled smart glasses.

“Everyone will have an exceptionally capable personal agent that understands you, your goals, and everything you care about,” Zuckerberg said. “You’ll be able to interact with your agent through any device, including your glasses to keep you present in the moment with the people you care about.”

On thornier issues such as loss of jobs from AI, autonomous weapons and government surveillance, Zuckerberg mostly brushed them aside. Law enforcement and the military already possess greater intelligence-gathering powers than the average person, Zuckerberg argued, and this would continue with access to AI. Companies may shrink in size due to AI, he conceded, but the technology would create new economic opportunities.

“People will have to adapt, and this will be challenging,” Zuckerberg said about labor disruption from new technology. “But the more that everyone has a personal agent that is superintelligent at teaching us new skills and helping us adapt to change, the smoother this will be.”

title: How to buy a bike: expert tips for finding the right budget, frame and fit
