title: Positive signs for Giants before late-game letdown leads to loss
description: San Francisco Giants starter Blade Tidwell was impressive after a slow start and outfielders Jung Hoo Lee and Drew Gilbert homered before Houston rallied to win at Oracle Park on Monday.
fullText:
Sometimes, the takeaways are more important than the results, especially for a team, such as the San Francisco Giants, well out of contention.

Solid to spectacular defense, excellent work from a young starter, a little situational hitting and a bit of power - all on the plus side of the ledger, especially Blade Tidwell's evening. Other positives: Jung Hoo Lee and Drew Gilbert homered for the Giants; Lee's was his career-high ninth, while Gilbert had his own tarps-off cheering section, his name spelled out on bare chests.

And then Dylan Smith, in to pitch the ninth, walked a batter and eventually wild-pitched pinch-runner Nick Allen to second. The Astros tied it on Cam Smith's two-out, two-strike groundball single through a big hole on the right side and Josh Hader set the Giants down in order in the bottom of the inning. Houston took the lead in the 10th when placed runner Smith went to third on Jason Foley's wild pitch, former Giants first baseman LaMonte Wade Jr. drew a pinch-hit walk and Jeremy Peña bounced a single through the drawn-in infield in the Astros' eventual 6-3 win.

Manager Tony Vitello called that inning "a big learning point to just learn how to navigate through those situations a little bit. Obviously, you don't want a walk, it's not ideal. No one's going to be flawless every time when they go out there, especially in those high-tension situations."

Vitello emphasized that the team is still trying to win games, even while taking a look at many young players. Still, it was hard not to be impressed by Tidwell, who is making a strong statement to be in next year's rotation. Recently dubbed "the Big Skittle" by Vitello, Tidwell allowed a run in the first but nothing else in his 5⅔ innings. That's two outings in a row in which opponents scored off Tidwell in the first and then he buttoned things up completely thereafter. That's both starts he's made since he was recalled Aug. 3.

a-walked for Vázquez in the 10th.

LOB: Houston 7, San Francisco 5. 2B: Alvarez (25), Paredes (21), Eldridge (15). HR: C.Smith (16), off Brubaker; Lee (9), off Wesneski; Gilbert (5), off Wesneski. RBIs: Altuve (35), C.Smith 2 (44), Peña (38), Paredes 2 (62), Gilbert 2 (24), Lee (46). SF: Altuve, Gilbert.

Runners left in scoring position: Houston 3 (Allen, Walker 2); San Francisco 3 (Cavanaugh, Lee, Devers). RISP: Houston 4 for 9; San Francisco 1 for 7.

Runners moved up: Adames. GIDP_Lee.

Inherited runners-scored: Brubaker 2-0. IBB_off Foley (Trammell). WP: D.Smith, Foley.

ABS Challenge: Tidwell (Ball-Overturned to Strike); Okert (Ball-Confirmed); McCray (Strike-Overturned to Ball).

Pitch timer violations: Foley (pitcher).

Umpires: Home, Mark Wegner; First, Steven Jaschinski; Second, Nate Tomlinson; Third, Paul Clemons.

Tidwell got 16 swings-and-misses Monday, including 12 with his sweeper, and he hit 98.3 mph with his fastball. He struck out six and walked just one.

"He was exceptional," Vitello said. He came out in the sixth with two outs and two on, and reliever JT Brubaker walked Taylor Trammell to load the bases. When Brubaker then went 3-2 on Christian Walker, Tidwell couldn't watch - cameras caught him hiding his face against his forearm as he watched while leaning on the dugout railing. Brubaker got Walker to ground out to end the inning.

"I'm one of those people that don't really get nervous whenever I'm doing something, but I get a little nervous when, like, my little cousin (is playing) basketball," Tidwell explained. "Yeah, I was spinning whenever I had my head down. I have faith in Bru."

Vitello, who also coached Tidwell at Tennessee, called Tidwell "the Big Skittle" before his previous start, explaining that he's rough on the outside but "a little softer on the inside than people realize." There's thought the nickname also might refer to Tidwell's current bare-noggin shaved-head look. .

Shortstop Willy Adames, coming on defensively after a slow start in the field and then a back injury that limited him somewhat, made a terrific play in the sixth, vacuuming up Peña's hard grounder up the middle, spinning and throwing to first, where Rafael Devers stretched for the bounce and got it with the extra effort. "Ridiculous," Vitello said of Adames' play. "And he definitely got some help."

Christian Koss, at third, made a good play on a slow grounder by Walker the previous inning. The entire outfield played well.

The Astros, too, got some super glovework, including Trammell's sliding grab in the fourth on Drew Cavanaugh's drive toward the gap in left - that ended the inning, leaving two men on. The Giants were 1-for-7 with runners in scoring position, including all three at-bats with the placed runner in the ninth.

Houston is the second American League team to visit Oracle Park on a roll after the Tigers. The Astros came in 40-28 since May 22 and in first place despite being just one game over .500 at 60-59.

title: Browns’ Demoted Starter Now ‘Fighting’ to Keep Roster Spot
description: The Cleveland Browns moved rookie Spencer Fano ahead of Dawand Jones at left tackle. Now, Jones is in some trouble. The post Browns’ Demoted Starter Now ‘Fighting’ to Keep Roster Spot appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Last week, things were looking up for veteran Cleveland Browns left tackle Dawand Jones. As there were questions about first-round draft pick Spencer Fano coming out of the gate in training camp, it appeared that the hard work Jones (who has started 20 games in three seasons) had put in to transform his body and get into better shape for the upcoming season was paying off. Jones spent much of the time in the opening days of camp working with the first team, and it looked as though he might beat out Fano for the starting job, at least to open the season.

Fano, according to Browns coaches, needed to get "up to speed."

Coach Todd Monken said last week, "I think there's a world in a number of spots where a player could end up starting while you get the other players up to speed. … (Dawand Jones) is in the best shape of his life. He's out there competing, talking smack, seems to be in a really good place, and we want to reward that. We also want to bring Spencer Fano along at a pace we feel is the best way to build his confidence."

Things change quickly in the NFL, of course. Fano had a notable practice on Saturday in which he went up against Pro Bowl edge rusher Jared Verse, and it got intense enough that the two scuffled. But Fano was impressive in that he did not back down from Verse thereafter, and held his own.

Thus, Fano was moved up to the first team. Now Jones is not only trying to win a job, but Monken pointed out that he's fighting for a spot on the roster. The Browns will likely carry 10 offensive lineman, and if he is not in the hunt for the starting left tackle job, Jones needs to show he is talented and versatile enough to be one of the 10.

Monken explained before Monday's practice that there is always competition for a player like Jones, who is entering his fourth season and still has much to prove:

"We're always competing, so he's been competing the whole time. I've been awfully proud of Dawand, what he's done in the offseason to get himself into shape and his body looks like it is. But at this point, Spencer is playing better. Now, once that happens, you're not just competing to maybe be the right tackle if something happens, maybe I'm still competing there. And you're also like, alright, once that happens, you're also competing for a roster spot.

"That's what you're doing at that point. Once you get to that point and you're thinking you should start competing your rear end off to get a roster spot. When you end up rotating with the twos, now you're fighting to make the team."

Again, as things stand, Jones is probably comfortably among the Top 10 lineman on the roster. But this is also a player who has been in just 24 games in three seasons, consistently snake-bitten by poorly timed injuries. It's doubtful that the Browns, with his contract up after this season, would keep him around if he got hurt again.

And there's also the massive shuffle that comes at the end of August in the NFL, when players are released form other teams. If the Browns' offensive staff–which has not been in place for Jones' tenure in Cleveland–sees some one set free whom they like better than Jones, his spot would be in peril.

It's been that kind of week for Dawand Jones.

title: Patriots Trade Rumors: Proposed Move to Send Key Weapon to the Chiefs
description: With a logjam of wide receivers, there have been trade rumors around the New England Patriots for months. Now, a new trade proposal would send one of the Patriots’ key weapons to the Kansas City Chiefs ahead of the 2026 season.Wynston Wilcox shared the proposal. In it, the Patriots would send Kayshon Boutte to the […] The post Patriots Trade Rumors: Proposed Move to Send Key Weapon to the Chiefs appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
With a logjam of wide receivers, there have been trade rumors around the New England Patriots for months. Now, a new trade proposal would send one of the Patriots' key weapons to the Kansas City Chiefs ahead of the 2026 season.

Wynston Wilcox shared the proposal. In it, the Patriots would send Kayshon Boutte to the Chiefs. Coming back would be a 2027 fourth-round pick.

"Kansas City should be very motivated to land Boutte," Wilcox wrote. "Even if a Tyreek Hill reunion was always a pipe dream, his recent injury update pretty much solidifies that he won't be playing much in 2026. With the need the Chiefs have at receiver, they can't wait around to land someone motivated to produce. Boutte is in a contract year, meaning he knows he has to have a good season to get a pay raise next spring."

There is going to be a major risk sending Boutte to a team like the Chiefs, who hope to bounce back from last season and be contenders in the AFC again. Run into them in the playoffs and let Boutte make a major play, and it could quickly become one of the most costly trades in modern Patriots history.

So, the Patriots need to ask themselves, is a fourth-round pick worth that risk? More than that, is a fourth-round pick worth the production that they'd lose by trading Boutte this season?

GettyNew England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte

It's been a phenomenal Training Camp so far for Kayshon Boutte. He and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye have been showing off their connection, particularly on deep balls, and he's making himself seem invaluable.

For Boutte, there is a reality that those trade rumors are hanging over his shoulders. So, he knows that whether it's in practice or a preseason game, this is tape his potential future team is judging him on.

"I mean, yeah. Every team pretty much watches," Boutte said. "They watch film. I wouldn't say practice film, but I mean they watch the game film. You see. Even preseason. Really, all 32 teams watching. Not just the team you play for… Everybody watching."

In three seasons with the Patriots, Boutte has 78 receptions for 1,159 yards and 9 touchdowns. That has included rapid improvement over the past two seasons. However, he's also entering the final year of his rookie contract and is due for a major pay raise. Given that the Patriots could very easily carry seven wide receivers, it makes sense to try and get something for Boutte rather than nothing.

"It's whatever's best for me," Boutte recently said. "Like I said, whether it's here or somewhere else, I gotta do what's best for me. I can't really say it today, you kinda gotta see how things play out. So like I say, taking it day by day, I'm not a future teller, so I couldn't tell you."

GettyNew England Patriots WR Kayshon Boutte

There's no doubt that Kayshon Boutte is the player hit hardest by the seemingly endless trade rumors. However, it has an effect on everyone, including Patriots quarterback Drake Maye as he tries to prepare for the season.

"He's here. He's here now," Maye said. "He's where his feet at, and I'm having fun throwing to him out there in practice. He's doing a great job, and he makes plays when the football is in the air. …That speaks for itself. I've had a lot of great times with Kayshon, and I'm looking forward to keep getting better each and every day."

For now, that's the pervasive thought within the Patriots. Focus as if Boutte is going to be with the team for the long run, and cross the bridge that is a trade if and when it comes to that.

title: Real Madrid defender will stay at the club next season despite fitness struggles
description: Real Madrid have spent big on the left-back department in recent summer transfer windows and have made two big-money signings, both of whom are worthy starters.Last summer, the club signed Alvaro Carr...
fullText:
Real Madrid have spent big on the left-back department in recent summer transfer windows and have made two big-money signings, both of whom are worthy starters.

Last summer, the club signed Alvaro Carreras for €50 million and they have gone on to sign Marc Cucurella for €55 million this time around. Both players remain at the club while Fran Garcia has left in search of more minutes.

A third left-back option who is currently at the club is Ferland Mendy, although the Frenchman has been battling recurrent injuries and is even currently on the sidelines.

Given his situation, a contract termination was seen as an option, but Diario AS now confirm that Real Madrid will not head down that approach this summer.

Indeed, as confirmed by the Spanish outlet, Mendy will stay at Real Madrid next season and is not planning on leaving the club either through a termination or a transfer.

Mendy will stay at the club. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

His current contract runs until 2028, and he thus has two more years left on his deal. Real Madrid respect the contract he signed and will not pressure him to leave. In fact, they have not even approached the player to ask him to look for a transfer or a termination.

If Mendy himself requests the club to leave, they will not pose any hurdles. But Real Madrid see him as a player who can add value when he is fully fit as matters stand.

The report also states that Mendy, for his part, is happy in Madrid and has no intention of leaving before his contract ends.

Mendy is happy in Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Injuries have not been kind to him, but he trusts that if he can stay fit, he can even return to the starting lineup. After all, he is a defensive specialist and would be invaluable in Jose Mourinho's system.

As matters stand, the player is expected to return to training in September and it remains to be seen if he can get any momentum on his side after that point. His recovery is currently going well, and the club's goal should be a long-term fix where the player can be of value.

title: Dana White Reacts to the Death of UFC Fighter Allan Nascimento
description: UFC president Dana White reacted to the tragic death of UFC flyweight fighter Allan Nascimento, who died on August 3.The UFC announced one week ago that Nascimento died of an apparent heart attack at age 34. His death came as a complete shock, as he appeared to be a healthy athlete who had just fought […] The post Dana White Reacts to the Death of UFC Fighter Allan Nascimento appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
UFC president Dana White reacted to the tragic death of UFC flyweight fighter Allan Nascimento, who died on August 3.

The UFC announced one week ago that Nascimento died of an apparent heart attack at age 34. His death came as a complete shock, as he appeared to be a healthy athlete who had just fought two months ago at UFC Vegas 119, when he dropped a split decision to Mitch Raposo.

A long-time training partner of UFC star Charles Oliveira at the Chute Boxe Diego Lima camp, Nascimento's death came as a complete shock and surprise to everyone in the MMA community, who were deeply saddened by losing one of their own.

Speaking to the media in Las Vegas following a tour of the newly revamped Meta Apex, White provided his first public comments about Nascimento's sudden death.

"It's horrible, and I know that his whole crew and team were literally devastated. These guys were so upset. It's just one of those freak, tragedy things that happen, and to a young guy who it shouldn't happen to," White said.

Nascimento was well loved by all of those who knew him, and his loss has left a huge hole in the hearts of his friends, fans, and family.

As White noted, Nascimento's team at Chute Boxe Diego Lima was devastated to hear of his passing. According to UFC commentator Daniel Cormier, Oliveira was supposed to fight Arman Tsarukyan in the co-main event of UFC 331 in September, but after hearing of Nascimento's passing, Oliveira was not able to take the fight, leading to Mauricio Ruffy stepping in and taking it.

A 29-fight MMA veteran, Nascimento began his mixed martial arts career in 2011 in his native Brazil. He then came to the United States and fought for Legacy FC (now LFA), and he also fought in Japan for RIZIN before competing on Dana White's Contender Series in 2018. Though he lost his fight on the show and didn't earn a UFC contract, he later got into the UFC, posting a 4-2 record overall.

title: Why Utah commit Dillon Sykes moved to Beehive State ahead of senior season
description: Elite receiver Dillon Sykes traded California for Lone Peak High to master his transition, build local bonds, and immerse himself in Salt Lake City’s culture before joining the Utes.
fullText:
Utah Utes football commit Dillon Sykes is officially leaving home.

The elite 6-foot-5 wide receiver has made the move from California to the Beehive State and will spend his senior season at Lone Peak High School before enrolling early at the University of Utah.

A lot of recruits commit to a school.

Not many move to that state nearly a year before they ever step on campus for their freshman year.

That's exactly what Sykes has done.

For Dillon, the move wasn't about leaving California behind. It was about getting a head start on the next chapter of his life and making the transition into Utah's program as smooth as possible.

Before the move, Sykes told me the decision came down to getting closer to the program, the coaching staff and the place he'll call home over the next several years.

"California is great. I love it here," Sykes said. "I appreciate everybody that's helped me here, but really it's just to get closer to the program, to the coaches, to everybody and make the adjustment easier."

California is where Sykes grew into one of Utah's top recruiting priorities. It's where he earned his first Power Four offer from the Utes and built the relationships that eventually led to his commitment.

Now, he's beginning the next step.

Before arriving in Utah, Sykes said he wanted the opportunity to become more familiar with both the state and the people around the program before officially becoming a college player.

"I just want to get more used to Utah, the state I'm going to be in for three, four, five years," Sykes said. "I want to see what they have to offer as a state. I really just want to see more, do more out there, get more involved."

The move also allows Sykes to spend his senior year around the program instead of following it from hundreds of miles away.

He'll be able to attend games at Rice-Eccles Stadium, continue building relationships with the coaching staff and play his final high school season just a short drive from Salt Lake City.

"I can go to the games more," Sykes said. "I heard the games are a great environment, and the coaches can come see me at any time. Every Friday night, wherever I am, I shouldn't be too far from Salt Lake."

"They can come see me. I can go see them and just continue to build the relationship and make this transition easier."

That relationship has always been one of the biggest reasons Utah separated itself.

The Utes were there early in Sykes' recruitment, and that held a lot of weight. Wide receivers coach Chad Bumphis believed in him, Morgan Scalley's vision connected with him, and the staff consistently made him feel like more than just another recruit.

When Sykes discussed the possibility of moving to Utah with the coaching staff, they fully supported the idea.

"They talked to me about it," Sykes said. "They said if I move out there, they would love it regardless of where I go. I can come see them. They can come see me. It'll just be an easier transition, and I can get to know everybody better."

There was also a little rivalry talk mixed into the conversations.

"They wanted me to stay away from the other team in Utah, so they wanted me to be closer to Salt Lake," Sykes said.

Dillon plans to graduate early, allowing him to make a short move north to campus once his high school career ends.

"As soon as I graduate high school, because I'll be an early grad, I'll probably just move 30 or 40 minutes away from where I was," Sykes said. "It's not too much of a big deal to me."

For Utah, the move is another example of just how invested Sykes is in the program.

The Utes found Dillon early, built genuine relationships, and ultimately earned his commitment after his official visit.

Now, before he has even signed his National Letter of Intent or stepped on campus as a student-athlete, Sykes has already made Utah home.

It's not something many recruits do.

But it says everything about how committed Dillon Sykes is to the future he's building with the Utes and is already on track to be a future Utah great.

title: Piastri’s 2026 struggles diagnosed as former McLaren driver reveals hidden problem
description: Oscar Piastri’s 2026 campaign has unfolded far differently from what was witnessed in 2025, and former McLaren driver Juan Pablo Montoya has pointed to a key factor behind the Australian’s struggles this season. Piastri, who led the Drivers’ Championship for more than 13 rounds during the 2025 season, has struggled to put together the consistency expected of him.
fullText:
Oscar Piastri's 2026 campaign has unfolded far differently from what was witnessed in 2025, and former McLaren driver Juan Pablo Montoya has pointed to a key factor behind the Australian's struggles this season.

Piastri, who led the Drivers' Championship for more than 13 rounds during the 2025 season, has struggled to put together the consistency expected of him. While the Australian has shown flashes of the form that made him a title contender last year, the 25-year-old has so far failed to match the pace of teammate Lando Norris.

Amid his difficult run through the first half of the season, Montoya has suggested that the manner in which Piastri lost the 2025 Drivers' Championship could be playing a major role in his current struggles.

The seven-time race winner believes the psychological impact of losing a title that appeared to be within Piastri's grasp could have affected his confidence and contributed to his dip in form.

Oscar Piastri has endured a challenging 2026 campaign so far - Photo: Race Pictures

"Losing the championship last year really hurt him mentally. It's a process of getting over it, figuring it out and getting the focus and the energy back on getting the job done. He is bloody good, so I think he will," Montoya said via a betting platform.

"It's such a big thing on the head, the psychology part of it. Losing the championship last year, everyone was talking like it was his, it was in the bag. When you're in that position where you look unbeatable and you lose the championship, it's a hard pill to swallow," he added.

Montoya, however, remains confident that Piastri can rediscover his best form, highlighting the Australian's natural speed and ability. "It's going to take some time to get back where he needs to be. He has the potential to do amazing things, I truly do. I think Oscar is a bloody good driver, he's very quick."

While Piastri sat comfortably at the top of the Drivers' Championship for much of the 2025 season before ultimately losing the title to teammate Norris, the Australian has managed just two podium finishes across the first 11 races of the 2026 campaign. His struggles were compounded at the Hungarian Grand Prix, where he failed to finish the race.

Earlier, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella identified what he believes has been the team's biggest lesson from a challenging opening half of the 2026 campaign.

Stella, who recently saw his squad return to victory lane for the first time since the 2025 Mexico City Grand Prix, highlighted unity and resilience as defining factors behind McLaren's ability to recover from a difficult start to the season.

Reflecting on the opening half of the campaign, the McLaren boss acknowledged the challenges the team has faced but praised the cohesion within the squad, insisting that its ability to regroup and respond has been crucial to its recovery. Stella also credited the resilience and contributions of both drivers, highlighting their role in helping McLaren turn its fortunes around following a difficult start to the season.

title: Following Guardiola and captaincy dilemma - Maresca on life at Man City
description: New Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca talks about replacing Pep Guardiola, his interest in AI and his captaincy dilemma.
fullText:
How do you replace Pep Guardiola?

Enzo Maresca is just starting to find out this summer, having been chosen as the Spaniard's successor at Manchester City - returning after being Guardiola's assistant during the club's Treble-winning 2022-23 campaign.

Guardiola, one of the greatest managers of his generation, stepped down at the end of last season after leading City to 17 major trophies, including six Premier League titles and a Champions League victory.

Now, with his first pre-season as manager at the club nearing its end, Maresca sat down with the five travelling UK-based media in Seoul to discuss the challenges ahead.

"After 10 games, if we have got 10 points, 20 points, 30 points. People will be comparing it to Pep after 10 games, it doesn't put pressure on me," said Maresca.

"I have said many times while I was at Leicester or Chelsea, he is the best manager in the world over the last 15 or 20 years.

"When he started in Spain, everyone wanted to play like Barcelona, he moved to Germany everyone wanted to play like Bayern [Munich], he comes to England and everyone wants to play like City.

"Someone asked me if it's the impossible job to follow him - maybe, but at the same time it's a privilege."

The ex-Chelsea boss says he met Guardiola in Barcelona a day before he officially signed as his replacement, as it was "useful" to pick his brains - having been at the club for a decade.

"We spent some hours together," he said. "We had planned before the season finished here to spend some time in the summer holidays together.

"I like to go in empty sometimes to see things for myself - but he was here so long, he has his opinions. But also you have to arrive and see things for yourself, see all the picture."

To signal a change for the players, Maresca has moved into the office of former assistant Pep Lijnders at City's headquarters, next door to Guardiola's old office - which has now been converted into a meeting room.

Shortly after his appointment as the City boss at the end of June, Maresca apologised to former club Chelsea for the "disruption" caused by his mid-season departure.

So what did he do during the intervening six months?

"I tried to enjoy a little bit more [time] with the family," he says about his wife and four children.

"And everyone is talking about AI, so I want to understand how it works. So I did two masterclasses to understand it a little bit more and have more knowledge."

Such has been the rise of artificial intelligence in everyday life, even Premier League managers are now beginning to dabble in it for those marginal gains.

But Maresca is going to need more than AI to make a success of his City career, having taken over from one of the greatest managers of his generation.

Marmoush double as Man City beat Atletico in Seoul

Man City reject Barcelona's £38.5m bid for Rodri

Maresca says the biggest difference in the Premier League from three years ago, when he was assistant to Guardiola, is the rise in set-pieces and teams defending man-to-man.

Last season, Arsenal claimed their first top-flight crown in more than two decades and scored 25 goals from set-pieces in the process - including 19 from corners alone - which is one aspect City are looking to "try to improve".

But rules for next season have been brought in, in an attempt to speed up the game - such as players having five seconds for goal-kicks and throw-ins, with possession handed over to the opposition if those limits are exceeded.

Despite the look of crowded penalty areas and jostling at corners seemingly taking away from the division stylistically, Maresca still feels it is the "best league" with the "best players".

He says: "It is because of the quality of the players, the quality of the managers, the organisation of the Premier League. It is completely different compared to other countries.

"Which league can compete with the Premier League? Spain? Barcelona, Real Madrid, yes, but then the rest is not the same. You have six teams here who are more or less there."

Maresca said he has not done an initiation song in front of the squad as "the manager doesn't sing".

He described goalkeeping coach Michele de Bernardin's performance as being "very good", while analyst Javi Molina's rendition of Frank Sinatra's My Way was "the worst".

The make-up of the backroom staff - with Argentine Willy Caballero, two Italians, three Spaniards and Maresca being able to speak French - means they have plenty of languages covered.

And then there is "the Englishman" - first-team coach Danny Walker, who was Maresca's assistant in City's elite development squad (EDS) and followed him to Leicester and Chelsea.

The manager is beaming when he discusses Walker. He says: "We go for breakfast it is beans on toast, we go for dinner it is a beer.

"When I joined the EDS, Danny was there, he was previously with the under-16s and they moved him to become my assistant. Since then we are always together, he knows Nico O'Reilly, Rico Lewis, he had them from under-six to under-12. He knows all of them.

"He is very good. He is good on extra work at the end, when we keep players doing something extra.

"It is demanding. If we don't win games, we are all going home."

Speaking of Englishmen, Maresca will choose the next City captain himself after Bernardo Silva's departure, and wants a homegrown player in the committee.

The leadership group currently consists of frontrunner Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland and Rodri, who has been the subject of a failed bid from Barcelona.

So is the Norway star a leading candidate to take the armband?

"Erling was one of the first to send a message when I joined the club," said Maresca.

"At Leicester and Chelsea I had a rule that when we scored the captain had to come to the bench, not to celebrate, but for instructions. But if he scores, then he can celebrate.

"If Erling is the captain, we have a problem, can you imagine? If you saw the game [against K-League XI] on Wednesday, when we scored the first goal, Ruben came over to the bench.

"I think even if it is two or three minutes, there is always something to adjust. At the moment, we have three or four [in the leadership group] and we are missing one. In the case of Rodri, see what happens."

The next captain, Rodri's future, City's starting XI for Sunday's Community Shield against Arsenal - the big decisions are stacking up as Maresca begins to settle into one of the biggest jobs on the planet.

title: 'Babar Azam is inexperienced': Pakistan told to shield captain from English media and send Shan Masood for interactions during England tour
description: Pakistan have been urged to limit Babar Azam’s media duties on the England tour, with Shan Masood suggested as the preferred choice for press interactions.
fullText:
'Babar Azam is inexperienced': Pakistan told to shield captain from English media and send Shan Masood for interactions during England tour originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Former Pakistan captain Rashid Latif wants the PCB to limit Babar Azam's English media interactions.

Latif believes Shan Masood is better suited for media duties due to his England experience.

Babar will captain Pakistan in a three-Test series against England from August 19.

Former Pakistan wicket-keeper batter Rashid Latif has recommended the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to protect Babar Azam from the English press as Pakistan prepares for a three-match Test series in England.

Babar has just been appointed as the new Pakistan Test captain and will lead the team in a tough assignment abroad, with the first match to be played against England at Headingley in Leeds, starting on August 19.

While commenting on Geo News' Score, Latif termed the England assignment tough, adding that the visiting team may come under additional pressure from the local press.

"An England tour is a difficult assignment, and the English media often tries to unnecessarily involve visiting teams in news stories," Latif added.

"Babar Azam is an experienced player, so it would be better for the PCB management to keep him away from the English media and send former captain Shan Masood to speak to them more often."

Rashid also proposed that Imam-ul-Haq and Mohammad Abbas would be suitable candidates to represent Pakistan in media engagements during the tour.

MORE:Will Babar reclaim PAK white-ball captaincy? Misbah rejects claim

Latif feels that Pakistan can lessen the burden on Babar Azam if Shan Masood is assigned a larger part in the media activities during the tour.

The reason cited by Latif for his suggestion was the experience that Masood already had of playing in England and handling the English media.

"Shan has played in England and has better experience of dealing with the English media," he stated.

The statement came at a time when Babar Azam is under immense media spotlight after being named the Test captain again.

Pakistan's two-test series against the West Indies ended in a draw and Babar made a crucial contribution as he led Pakistan to their first away Test win in over three years.

MORE:Hardik Pandya trade: Which team will sign MI captain?

Pakistan face England after a 1-1 draw in the West Indies Tests. Babar was not out for 58 runs in the first Test loss but got 88 runs in the first innings of the second Test and was not out for 24 in the successful chase.

The eight-wicket win in the second Test was particularly important for Pakistan because it helped end their eight-game losing run abroad and Babar get his first overseas Test win as a captain.

The English series is bound to be a much harder challenge for Pakistan. The first Test of Pakistan against England will begin from August 19 to 23 at Headingley, followed by the second Test from August 27 to 31 at Lord's and third from September 9 to 13 at Edgbaston.

The Test series is set to be Pakistan's first in England since 2020 and comes under the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 cycle.

MORE:When Sangakkara accused Indians of 'cheating': Pathan recalls heated chat

Even if Latif's idea sounds bizarre, there is some sense in this. Babar is not necessarily required to be the most prominent figure in the media of the team just because he is the captain.

An experienced player like Shan Masood can shoulder some media responsibility, which would be beneficial, taking into account his experience of playing in England and dealing with the English media, allowing Babar to focus on his captaincy and batting.

Nevertheless, it may prove impossible to protect Babar from the English media as well as unnecessary to do so, since being captain of the team, Babar is destined to answer questions regardless of whether his team plays well or not.

Flagg personally unveiled and signed his Rookie Debut Patch Autograph during Fanatics Fest in July. The card contains a game-worn patch tied to his first NBA game and is the only copy of that particular card in existence.

Topps made Rookie Debut Patch Autographs one of the centerpieces of 2025-26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball, highlighting Flagg alongside Kon Knueppel and Dylan Harper. Every Rookie Debut Patch Auto is a one-of-one.

Heavy had been tracking whether Flaggâs card had surfaced since the productâs August 6 release.

It has now surfaced â and that may only begin the most interesting part of its story.

The Mavericks announced their pursuit of the card on August 6.

Dallasâ package is headlined by two premium lower-level season tickets covering the next 32 years, a number matching Flaggâs No. 32 jersey. The team also included game-worn memorabilia, private experiences involving Flagg and a Mavericks road trip to Boston.

It is an unusual offer because its value cannot be judged strictly like a cash bounty.

A collector could theoretically value decades of premium Mavericks seats and access to Flagg more highly than someone primarily interested in maximizing the cardâs immediate market value. And Dallas isn't the only interested party.

Auction executive Ken Goldin has already put a very different seven-figure proposal on the table.

Goldin said his company would give whoever pulled the card a $1.5 million cash advance for consigning it to Goldin, then take the card to auction and attempt to produce a substantially larger sale. Heavy broke down Goldinâs $1.5 million Flagg card proposal before the card was found.

That distinction matters: Goldin is not simply offering $1.5 million to buy the card. He described the money as an advance connected to an eventual consignment and auction, and said Goldin would attempt to get the owner $3 million, $4 million or even $5 million. He did not publicly detail all of the financial terms governing the advance.

There is another wrinkle that makes this particular chase different from a typical high-dollar rookie pull: Flagg himself has shown a genuine interest in cards.

The Mavericks star revealed during an appearance with Kevin Hart that he and his cousin are starting their own sports card shop back home, although he had not yet announced its name, exact location or opening date at the time.

Flagg has also already become the subject of several unusual hobby releases. Earlier in his rookie season, Topps produced a one-of-one Flagg-Kon Knueppel dual autograph card containing pieces of game-worn sneakers from their memorable Mavericks-Hornets matchup.

That hobby momentum arrived alongside a historic rookie season. Flagg ultimately won Rookie of the Year after averaging 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists, after Heavy had tracked his late Rookie of the Year push and the injury that ended his rookie season.

The card chase, however, had one question hanging over it from the moment Flagg signed the one-of-one at Fanatics Fest: Who would find it?

That question has finally been answered.

The next one could be worth considerably more: What will its owner do with it?

Reeling fromRodri's rejection, Real Madrid have decided the midfielder market is not for them this summer. According to Diario AS, the Spanish side believe there isn't a single midfielder available on the market who is capable of improving their squad.

Eli Kroupi Junior is a player of interest, though the Bournemouth forward's broken foot has scuppered that move. title: The huge task facing Enzo Maresca at Man City as shadow of the past looms large
description: Replacing Pep Guardiola will be no mean feat for former Man City assistant Maresca but the challenges extend beyond just the size of the shoes that need filling
fullText:
In their first season after Pep Guardiola stood down, Barcelona won the Spanish league. In their first season after Pep Guardiola left, Bayern Munich won the German league. And so, in their first season after Pep Guardiola walked away, Manchester City will…?

The precedents may be encouraging but the reality is that, even as they mounted a Premier League title challenge last season, City finished seven points behind Arsenal, after ending up 13 adrift of Liverpool the previous year. Guardiola left City as their greatest ever manager, but with his greatest side being broken up, a process that continued with the summer departures of John Stones and the captain Bernardo Silva.

Enzo Maresca, a replacement that offers echoes of Tito Vilanova – another sidekick in a Champions League-winning campaign – was Guardiola's assistant in the treble campaign of 2022-23, but inherits a very different side.

The Italian returns to the Etihad having called Guardiola the best manager of the last 20 or 25 years and noted Manchester United and Arsenal's difficulties after the departures of Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger respectively. His is a formidably tough task in one respect but at least, Maresca may console himself, he no longer has to deal with BlueCo at Chelsea.

The fact that it took a £17m compensation package to bring in Maresca – six months after he left Chelsea – and delayed his appointment, underlined that City's summer has been expensive and awkward at times. They had a World Cup-winning captain in the squad, and Rodri would have seemed the logical successor to Silva with the City armband, except that he is in the last year of his contract, wanted by Real Madrid and subject of a £38.4m bid from Barcelona. He may be on the brink of going. It could leave City having broken the transfer record for a British player this summer and yet with a weaker midfield, if they lose both Silva and Rodri.

All of which may indicate City have less allure – even to the players they already own – without Guardiola. A team that was definitively too old in 2024-25 could look young now. The rebuilding job has been costly, with almost £700m spent in the last four transfer windows and perhaps more to come in the next few weeks, but is unfinished. Maresca has targeted full-back additions and, if Rodri goes, a midfielder could be required, with Morocco's Ayyoub Bouaddi and Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez both of interest.

City have started to shape Maresca's side, though. The £116m deal for Elliot Anderson secured their top target, with the added bonus that Manchester United also wanted him. Josko Gvardiol, Abdukodir Khusanov and Phil Foden have signed new contracts; if the Mancunian could recapture the form that earned him the Footballer of the Year award and yielded 27 goals in 2023-24, it would be a triumph for Maresca, though Foden ended last season without a goal in 29 games and losing his place to Rayan Cherki.

City's overhaul leaves them better stocked in some areas than others. In Gvardiol and Khusanov, plus Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias, they have four quality centre-backs, giving the possibility the Croatian or the Uzbek may be used on the flanks. Gianluigi Donnarumma became a fixture in goal, with the consequence that James Trafford left a year after rejoining; City's capacity to bring in high fees was shown by a £45m deal.

Elsewhere, however, it will be intriguing who Maresca prefers. Erling Haaland's importance is a given to such an extent that he scored 38 goals last season and didn't finish in the top three of City's player-of-the-year vote. Nico O'Reilly won it; does Maresca see him as more of a left-back or a midfielder, though?

Some of the acquisitions in the last couple of years spent much of Guardiola's last few months on the bench, in Nico Gonzalez, Tijjani Reijnders, Omar Marmoush and Savinho. In the case of the Brazilian, in particular, it was because Jeremy Doku kicked on and Antoine Semenyo arrived.

The broader picture is that City recruited a group of fine players; but if part of the challenge is to construct a team, part of the problem is that some of their predecessors, and men Maresca coached, were great players.

That will be an issue for the Italian: the shadow of the past, whether Guardiola himself or an all-conquering team who set standards that are hard to match. In the Catalan's last couple of years, City lacked the consistency they had shown in the past. Their fortunes tailed off in the Champions League, with exits in the knockout phase play-offs and the round of 16. They kept facing Real Madrid, but they also lost to too many others.

They nevertheless displayed a potency in one-off games. They did a cup double last season, beating eventual champions Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final and the Chelsea that Maresca left behind in the FA Cup showpiece.

The Italian took Chelsea to fourth in his only full season in charge and left them in fifth. His greatest feat, like City's in Guardiola's valedictory year, came in knockout competitions. Maresca won the Club World Cup with the Blues.

When he was last at City, and in a more meaningful sense, they became the best team in the world. They are not now; but as Maresca tries to restore them to those heights, part of the task is to rival another of Guardiola's old assistants, in Mikel Arteta, part is to prove a worthy successor to a legend and part is to avoid the fate of David Moyes at United and Unai Emery at Arsenal.

title: Vikings Quietly Exploring Another Option for Their Backfield
description: The Minnesota Vikings worked out former Detroit Lions running back Jermar Jefferson. This was reported by the NFL’s daily transaction wire on Monday afternoon.Jefferson was originally drafted by the Lions in the seventh round of the 2021 NFL draft. He spent most of his time with the Lions between the active roster and the practice […] The post Vikings Quietly Exploring Another Option for Their Backfield appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Minnesota Vikings worked out former Detroit Lions running back Jermar Jefferson. This was reported by the NFL's daily transaction wire on Monday afternoon.

Jefferson was originally drafted by the Lions in the seventh round of the 2021 NFL draft. He spent most of his time with the Lions between the active roster and the practice squad. Over the course of his career, he has also played with the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals. Both of those came last season. He was able to make a minor impact with the Cardinals, appearing in two games on special teams.

Jefferson has recorded 21 rushing attempts for 96 yards and two touchdowns. The playmaker has also tallied five receptions for 33 yards. Now, the Vikings brought him in to see if he could add to their strong running back room.

Jefferson had a successful college career. He played for the Oregon State Beavers from 2018 to 2020. Jefferson began his career strong, appearing in 12 games for the Beavers in 2018. He recorded 239 carries for 1,380 yards and 12 touchdowns. This included 254 rushing yards against Arizona State. Jefferson was named the Pac-12 Freshman Offensive Player of the Year for his efforts.

2020 was another season in which he was able to showcase his talents. His junior season saw him record 143 rushing yards per game and 6.5 yards per carry. All told, he tallied 133 carries for 858 yards and six touchdowns in six games. Jefferson was named the Co-Pac-12 Offensive Player of the Year and received first-team All-Pac-12 honors.

The proof of Jefferson's skill set was in the games he played. He had 1500-yard rushing games over 27 career appearances. It was easy to see why NFL teams wanted to take a chance on him.

The 2026 calendar year has been busy for him. He was signed by the San Francisco 49ers on May 28 to a one-year contract. He was waived just five days later on June 2. Jefferson also had a workout with the Green Bay Packers on July 27. This was a depth move on the part of the Packers as well. They were also able to see if he could help their team.

Now, the Vikings brought in Jefferson. The running back position is an interesting one for the Vikings, as Aaron Jones undoubtedly leads the way. Jordan Mason and Demond Claiborne also provide support. Claiborne in particular has had an intriguing training camp. The rookie has emerged as a pleasant surprise at the position, and could factor in heavily to the rotation sooner rather than later. The emergence of Claiborne has made it so running back depth is necessarily the most pressing need.

With that being said, it is never a bad thing to try and check off boxes and add players for depth purposes. This is exactly what the preseason is all about. If anything, the Vikings are doing a little bit of homework with their first preseason game on Thursday.

The offense has a chance to be explosive in the fall, and adding additional depth may be what is needed to get over the hump.

title: Trump says would be 'terrible mistake' to oust embattled Infantino
description: US President Donald Trump said on Monday it would be "a terrible mistake" to replace Gianni Infantino, the embattled FIFA president who tried, and failed, to sell off part of the World Cup to private investors."FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino," Trump posted on Truth Social.
fullText:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday it would be "a terrible mistake" to replace Gianni Infantino, the embattled FIFA president who tried, and failed, to sell off part of the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino came under renewed fire in an open letter signed by three confederations -- Europe's UEFA, North and Central America's CONCACAF and Asia's AFC -- accusing the world football boss of breaking trust "through deception".

But Trump backed Infantino, who awarded the US president a "FIFA Peace Prize" at the World Cup draw ceremony last year.

"FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino," Trump posted on Truth Social.

Trump called Infantino "fantastic" and said he "presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented".

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!" added Trump, who attended the World Cup final with Infantino last month.

Trump's backing of Infantino is at odds with US Soccer, who joined the voices lining up against the FIFA president.

Infantino launched, and then withdrew in the face of scathing criticism, a plan to bring private investment into FIFA competitions, including World Cups.

FIFA hit back on Saturday at efforts "to undermine" football's governing body and Infantino.

However, Monday's joint letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC retorted: "Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding -- or demanding -- power to be held.

"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned."

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is viewed as a potential challenger to Infantino, who will be up for re-election for a fourth and final term at the FIFA Congress in March, 2027. Candidates have to be declared by November 18.

Infantino had looked certain to be unopposed for a fourth term after overseeing a successful World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada until his plans were revealed.

The 56-year-old Swiss, who has been in situ for 10 years, has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive.

Individual member associations, not confederations, vote in the FIFA election,

Infantino has received support from CONCACAF's Mexico and two AFC members -- Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar, where he has a house.

UEFA's threat to boycott World Cups if the private investment plan went ahead proved pivotal in Infantino withdrawing his sell-off plan.

UEFA had called it "a shabby, opaque, backroom deal" and lashed out at Infantino again on Monday for a "failure of judgment".

After the furore, Infantino received "full support" of senior FIFA directors in an emergency meeting in Morocco last week, but the three confederations said that was meaningless.

The recent meeting, where "a select number of members of the FIFA Management Committee" were present, they said, "represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment".

"It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him."

Infantino had been basking in the afterglow of the largest ever World Cup involving 48 teams until his plans divided the sport.

"The growth over the past decade has been real. But that progress was never the work of one individual," declared the letter.

"It was the product of FIFA, the Confederations, the Member Associations, and the thousands of people who dedicate their lives to the game.

"The expanded tournaments... were shared achievements, agreed together, delivered together."

Under Infantino's leadership "there is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness", they said.

"That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve.

"Football's strength has always been its unity."

title: Jason Whitlock claims Sophie Cunningham is a player the WNBA is 'built to isolate'
description: Jason Whitlock is not happy with the way the WNBA has handled the situation with Sophie Cunningham. Cunningham has become somewhat of a lightning rod both on and off the court in the WNBA.
fullText:
Jason Whitlock is not happy with the way the WNBA has handled the situation with Sophie Cunningham.

Cunningham has become somewhat of a lightning rod both on and off the court in the WNBA. Her role as one of the enforcers on the Indiana Fever made her a polarising figure for many fans.

But in recent weeks, Cunningham's comments on the trans athlete issue have made her an even more controversial presence in the league than before.

Speaking on his show, Jason Whitlock addressed DiJonai Carrington's hard foul on Sophie Cunningham and suggested that it was a way to retaliate against Cunningham for her outspoken stance on the trans athlete debate.

Whitlock claimed that Cunningham is being silenced by the WNBA's 'sisterhood' for not aligning herself with the moral values the league tries to present to the world.

"Sophie will not bend the knee on men in women's sports. Sophie will not run the approved script after she gets her mouth bloodied.

"So Sophie is not 'sisterhood' material. She is content. She is a problem to manage. She is the woman the machine is built to isolate.

"DiJonai Carrington is not the random villain of the week. She is the perfect instrument of this culture… She wears her politics on her chest. Activist posture, quick to the culture war."

Speaking further on the matter, Whitlock suggested that Carrington's refusal to apologise to Cunningham for the foul was a clear sign that she was working to protect the state media-endorsed narrative.

"When the trans athlete fight heated up around Sophie's public stance, Carrington did not stay out of it; she stepped in. Then she stepped into Sophie at the rim.

"When the ejection hit, she did not apologise to the woman with her blood in her mouth; she posted 'White Privilege' in all caps. That is the whole ideology.

"Hurt a woman outside the circle, then accuse her of systemic advantage… Sophie is the victim of the foul and the defendant in the narrative. That system only works if the media runs it for you."

Whitlock has long been a staunch critic of the WNBA for their refusal to condemn the progressive politics of many of their players.

For him, seeing Cunningham become one of the pre-eminent voices in the trans athlete debate was a huge plus.

Even though the rhetoric surrounding the WNBA does not make any sense given that there are no trans athletes in the league or any who have attempted to enter the league.

But that hasn't stopped Whitlock and other voices like him from discussing this issue and crafting a narrative against the WNBA.

title: Fact Check: FAKE Video Shows DiJonai Carrington Saying Sophie Cunningham Should Be Charged With Assault For Trying To Pull Off Her Wig
description: Is a video authentic that shows Chicago Sky player DiJonai Carrington saying Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham should be charged with assault for nearly pulling off her wig? No, that's not true: The video is AI-generated. An online detection tool...
fullText:
Is a video authentic that shows Chicago Sky player DiJonai Carrington saying Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham should be charged with assault for nearly pulling off her wig? No, that's not true: The video is AI-generated. An online detection tool found the video was 81.4% likely AI-generated. There are no credible news reports of Carrington making the accusation against Cunningham.

The claim appeared in an Aug. 9, 2026, video posted on X account @FeverUpdate (archived here). It opened:

Dijonai Carrington claims Sophie Cunningham nearly pulled off her wig during their altercation.

'She should be charged with assault for trying to take off my wig.'

This is what the post looked like on X at the time of writing:

This is what the video looked like on X at the time of writing:

Dijonai Carrington claims Sophie Cunningham nearly pulled off her wig during their altercation.

"She should be charged with assault for trying to take off my wig." pic.twitter.com/FBbJk66C1y

Lead Stories uploaded the video clip to Hive Moderation (pictured below), which determined the video was 81.4% likely to be AI-generated.

Lead Stories searched Google News and Yahoo News for the phrase, "Dijonai Carrington Sophie Cunningham wig assault" and did not find any matching results of Carrington on video saying Cunningham should be charged with assault for trying to pull off her wig. The search did find a report on People.com of Carrington being ejected from the Aug. 8, 2026, game after fouling Cunningham and posting a message on her Threads account @dijonai that read "WHITE PRIVILEGE."

title: Four-Time NFL Pro Bowler Praises Dave Roberts Gesture Before Dodgers Game
description: The Dodgers manager got praised for this kind gesture that sparked a reaction from a past NFL star. The post Four-Time NFL Pro Bowler Praises Dave Roberts Gesture Before Dodgers Game appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers draw out celebrities for literally every home game. That included a past four-time Pro Bowler in the NFL Monday. Yet former Las Vegas Raiders and New Orleans Saints quarterback Derek Carr couldn't help but praise a kind gesture manager Dave Roberts made.

Carr took his family to see the Dodgers on the field before facing the Kansas City Royals at Chavez Ravine. But he took to the social media website X, formerly known as Twitter, to share the action Roberts made before the game while underneath an 88 degree sky before the opening pitch.

"Shoutout to Dave Roberts. We are at a Dodgers game and he noticed my wife holding our newborn and kids in the heat during batting practice. He invited us into his office to cool off for 30 minutes," Carr posted.

Carr added that Roberts is a "genuinely kind person. Thanks Dave. Go Dodgers." Carr also is in Los Angeles for another reason, though.

The Bakersfield, California native is soon going to make Westwood his newest work home.

UCLA football has named Carr to the 2026 coaching staff under new head coach Bob Chesney. So now he'll serve as a special advisor while helping with game-planning and assiting the quarterbacks. The school made that announcement on Monday before Carr took in the Dodgers game.

"We are excited to welcome Derek to our program," Chesney said in a school news release. "He has played the quarterback position at a high level for more than a decade, and his experience, leadership and football knowledge will be an incredible resource for our coaching staff and student-athletes."

Chesney added what he loved about Carr in making the official hire.

"What stands out most is his passion for the game and his commitment to developing young people. Derek will have a tremendous impact on our players and is a great addition to our program," Chesney adds.

The 11-year NFL quarterback holds no previous ties to the Big Ten university. He never was recruited by UCLA either out of Bakersfield Christian High School.

However, he's got ties to general manager Darrick Yray, who was at Fresno State with Carr during his illustrious collegiate run. Yray helped endorse Carr's hire to UCLA while the retired NFL quarterback raved about this opportunity.

"The opportunity to help Coach Chesney, the staff and the quarterbacks at UCLA was one that really excited me," Carr said via UCLA. "I'm looking forward to sharing my experiences and helping support the program in any way I can."

Now taking in Dodger games amid this playoff push comes with the work perks for Carr.

Los Angeles dealt with a sudden skid that made fans and analysts hit the panic button. Even newcomer pitcher from the Detroit Tigers Tarik Skubal took a loss to the Chicago Cubs in his LA debut.

LA managed to end a sudden seven-game slide against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Saturday 2-1. But Arizona snatched Sunday's game with a 4-2 score.

Roberts is aiming to redeem this team after losing eight of their last nine contests.

Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us.

title: Rays Rally Past Athletics for Seventh Straight Win, Extend AL East Lead
description: The Tampa Bay Rays won their seventh straight game with a 10-6 comeback victory over the Athletics. Freddy Peralta bounced back in his second Rays start, while Junior Caminero's 34th home run helped Tampa Bay extend its AL East lead to six games.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Rays just keep winning.

On Monday, the team picked up their seventh straight win as they continue to be unbeaten on the road during this West Coast trip, taking down the Athletics 10-6 in Sacramento.

There were a lot of things to be excited about for Kevin Cash and his roster. Here's what you need to know from the contest.

After a nightmare debut for Tampa Bay following being acquired at the MLB trade deadline, Freddy Peralta bounced back nicely Monday in Sacramento. He wasn't flawless, but he didn't have to be. He allowed six hits across six innings, struck out five, and gave up three earned runs, with two coming in the first inning.

After the opening frame, he settled in nicely. The only other deviation came in the bottom of the fifth inning when Zack Gelof sent a solo home run to give the Athletics an early lead.

Other than a solo home run from Yandy Diaz in the top of the first inning, the bats started slow for Tampa Bay. However, after the Athletics got up to a 6-2 lead in the bottom of the seventh inning, the Rays turned on the jets. The team picked up 8 unanswered runs, beginning with a three-run home run by Junior Caminero, his 34th of the season.

The home run couldn't come at a better time for Caminero, as he was struggling at the plate. Maybe the long ball will help him regain some confidence. He finished the day going 1 for 5 with the homer.

The team responded in a big way by getting a ton of base traffic against the Athletics' pitchers, and when they got traffic, they capitalized. The team was 5 for 13 with runners in scoring position, helping them gain double digits in the run column.

With the team picking up their seventh straight win, they now pull ahead by six games of the New York Yankees for the American League East division lead. They are also up by eight games on the Boston Red Sox after their recent three-game losing streak. This is exactly what Tampa Bay needed during this stretch of games.

The team is currently facing multiple organizations with losing records and will not face a winning team until the last weekend of the month. While Tampa Bay is away from Tropicana Field, a place they have played very well in 2026, they had to capitalize, and so far they clearly have. The team is now 31-28 on the road and 72-46 on the season.

They will look for consecutive win number 8 as they take on the Athletics in the second game of the series. On Tuesday, Nick Martinez will get the start. He'll take on right-hander Mason Barnett for the Athletics. First pitch is scheduled for 9:40 p.m. Eastern.

title: Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino
description: US President Donald Trump says it would be a "terrible mistake" if under pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted.
fullText:
US President Donald Trump says it would be a "terrible mistake" if under pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted from his position.

Trump's backing followed Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) issuing an open letter accusing Infantino of breaking trust "through deception" with his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Trump's comments are the first time he has come out in defence of Infantino since the FFE plans came to light on 28 July.

"Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino," Trump wrote on social media.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again."

The 2026 World Cup was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico this summer, with Spain crowned champions after beating Argentina in the final.

When addressing the FFE proposals for the first time on 31 July, Trump said he had not spoken to Infantino about the plans.

Thrive Eternal was expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Infantino has a close relationship with Trump and awarded him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize in December 2025.

Infantino broke trust 'through deception' - confederation presidents

Fifa scraps controversial World Cup investment plan

European football's governing body Uefa has threatened a boycott of all Fifa competitions, as well as saying it could take legal action over the failed FFE plans.

The letter issued by Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC - the three confederations representing Europe, North America, Central America and the Caribbean, and Asia - came after Fifa said there was a "concerted and ongoing effort" to "undermine" world football's governing body and Infantino.

BBC Sport understands that there have been preliminary discussions between the three confederations over breakaway competitions, should Infantino remain in his position. However, substantive talks are yet to begin, according to others.

"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned," the letter from Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC read.

While the statement did not name Infantino, sources have told BBC Sport that it should be seen as an opportunity for him to resign and leave his position with dignity.

title: Real Madrid forward will not leave on loan this summer, has manager and club president’s backing
description: After selling Gonzalo Garcia and signing Carlos Espi, it looked set that Jose Mourinho would count on Real Madrid’s new striker as his backup to Kylian Mbappe next season. The manager, after all, va...
fullText:
After selling Gonzalo Garcia and signing Carlos Espi, it looked set that Jose Mourinho would count on Real Madrid's new striker as his backup to Kylian Mbappe next season. The manager, after all, values the profile of a natural number nine for certain game states.

The club's decision to sign Espi, however, sent a loud and clear message to Endrick who was hoping to take over the same role after returning from loan.

In the weeks that followed, uncertainty around his future grew with increasing rumours that he could leave on loan this summer. Aston Villa and Roma were the two big parties alert to the possibility and were willing to welcome him on an immediate loan.

As confirmed in a recent update by Diario AS, Real Madrid have now made a final decision on Endrick's immediate future and have definitively shut down the idea of him leaving on loan. He will stay at Real Madrid for the beginning of the new season.

Jose Mourinho counts on Endrick. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Jose Mourinho counts on the player and believes that he can have a relevant role in the team in the coming campaign despite the arrival of Espi.

Florentino Perez also shares the same opinion and has a special fondness for Endrick given his talent, age and the fee they paid for him.

The player is willing to accept the challenge of staying and fighting for his spot, and will thus remain in the Spanish capital.

Mourinho hopes to use Endrick not only as a backup centre-forward but also as a possible backup right-wing option if the need arises. After all, the player has played in that position in the past.

Endrick will not leave on loan. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

The coming six months, thus, will be critical in deciding the long-term future of Endrick. It remains to be seen what position, and to what capacity the manager trusts the player.

As matters stand, the Brazilian star has not ruled out leaving on loan in January if his situation does not improve. After all, he had a positive experience on loan at Olympique Lyon and is not opposed to taking that route if he is not given enough minutes in Madrid.

title: Inside the transgender controversy taking over the WNBA, from Sophie Cunningham’s comments to now
description: WNBA discourse has been recently dominated by the ongoing debate about whether transgender athletes should be allowed in women’s sports, and it’s interesting to see how it got to this point. The WNBA has gotten caught up in a larger cultural issue over the past couple of weeks.
fullText:
WNBA discourse has been recently dominated by the ongoing debate about whether transgender athletes should be allowed in women's sports, and it's interesting to see how it got to this point.

The WNBA has gotten caught up in a larger cultural issue over the past couple of weeks. The topic in question? Whether transgender athletes should be allowed to compete in women's sports.

This culture war controversy has been going on for a long time within the world of sports. But considering that the W has been known for its inclusivity, it hadn't come up in the league's context yet.

However, all that changed with Sophie Cunningham's July comments, which opened up a Pandora's box and led to a chain reaction. Here's a look at the timeline of the entire debate.

Cunningham's rise to WNBA stardom came suddenly after her hard foul while defending superstar Caitlin Clark, and she has only grown more popular since.

In 2022, Cunningham had reposted a comment protesting transgender swimmer Lia Thomas. The backlash on social media was swift, and she released a statement expressing support for all athletes.

Her comments which sparked this recent argument came in an ESPN interview published on July 21.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans," Cunningham said. "And I'm like, 'I never once said that,'" she says. "I think that I am here to extend love.

"But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

This led to many fans praising for speaking 'the truth' despite it being controversial. Others felt the comments were a bit intolerant and against exclusivity, which led to others in the league speaking out.

The league has long been known as a queer-friendly, inclusive space in the world of sports. It was natural that the Fever player's comments would lead to a response.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve wore a t-shirt in support of transgender people, it read, 'Trans kids belong'. And speaking ahead of the Lynx-Fever clash earlier in August, she explained her point.

"I come from a space of inclusion," Reeve told reporters, as per an ESPN report. "The narrative that I think is problematic is to suggest that transgender athletes are the biggest problem in women's sports.

"This is what's bothersome. There is a faction of people in our country that are making this a massive issue."

Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase added her voice to this view as well.

"For me sports is about belonging," Nakase said. "It's about inclusivity. It's about allowing everyone to be their authentic self. I'm all about women, little girls deserving to play, and that includes trans women."

The two coaches' comments also received pushback, Stephen A. Smith was among those to call out Reeve. While the controversy was only raging within the league at this point, it was about to get some new entrants.

This issue has caused ripples all over the sports world, and some former NBA stars saw the opportunity to involve themselves. Enes Kanter Freedom was the first to do so, wildly declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft.

"After careful consideration and reviewing the current eligibility guidelines, I'm officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect," Freedom wrote in a post on X.

If simply declaring who you are is all that's required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA… Based on the current guidelines, I can and am officially declaring my eligibility for the upcoming WNBA draft."

He wasn't the only person with this idea either, Royce White followed suit just hours later, claiming the same thing.

"I'm transgender. I'm a woman. I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball, professional basketball, so I'll be declaring for the WNBA draft in 2027 as well," White said.

The involvement of Freedom and White took the issue to a whole new level. Both have since only doubled down on their messaging, fanning the flames of an already heated social media debate.

The million-dollar question for the WNBA is where things go from here. The WNBPA has already released a statement announcing their stance against discrimination and athletes being excluded.

"Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm," the statement reads.

"We will continue to have hard conversations. But we will not be used as political pawns."

The players seem committed to keeping the WNBA inclusive, but the situation might force the league to define their policies in one way or another.

It's a shame that a political issue seems to be overshadowing the game on the court at the moment. Hopefully, the situation will be dealt with soon and fans can get excited for some playoff hoops instead.
